chapters.title: Chapter 976: Straightforward
paragraphs: Wei Man held a suitcase and kept running. She only stopped to catch her breath when she saw the sign of the Emergency Medical Center ahead of her. She checked the time and thought, ‘Luckily, I’m not late.’

Since Yun Hua Hospital built the Emergency Medical Center, its requirements for the standards of emergency consultation had also increased. The requirement for doctors from other departments to arrive at the latest within ten minutes remained unchanged from the past, but now, a requirement for them to arrive within eight minutes had also been added to serve as the first borderline.

If a doctor could reach in eight minutes, good comments would be left in his or her record. Ten minutes was still considered normal, and anyone who took more than ten minutes to arrive would fail to meet the requirement. When this procedure was implemented, most of the doctors could reach within eight minutes, thus the borderline of eight minutes had now become the maximum amount of time allowed for doctors to arrive.
No department director would want their record to be worse than the record of others.

However, when the doctors in each department truly had to implement it, the pressure on them inevitably increased largely because the acceptable amount of time they had to reach the Emergency Department had been reduced by two minutes. This meant that once the doctors received the call, they needed to rush over to the Emergency Medical Center, and they needed to deal with all the obstacles they met on the way quickly.

Wei Man was the attending physician on duty in the Department of Urology today. She had to explain the situation to the family member of a patient with kidney stones, which was why she was in a bit of a hurry. As the lift was not efficient, she ran over using the stairs.
Ma Yanlin knew that his wife was the person on duty in the Department of Urology today. He felt sorry for his wife and waited for her outside. He immediately waved at her when he saw her.
“I’m not late, right?” Wei Man was still quite serious when she was working. She spoke in a business-like tone when she saw Ma Yanlin.

“No,” Ma Yanlin quickly replied and lowered his voice to say, “A boiler in the industrial park exploded. There are six seriously wounded patients being sent over now, and there should still be some other patients as well.”
Wei Man nodded slowly and looked at Ling Ran, who was in the frontmost row. She subconsciously said, “Thankfully, Doctor Ling is on duty today.”
“I know, right?” Ma Yanlin immediately replied and spoke out of concern for her again, “Are you the only one from your department? The third-string doctors were informed, right?”

“They were definitely informed. Associate Chief Physician Guo will come over soon,” Wei Man said in a flirtatious tone and rolled her eyes at Ma Yanlin. “You’re just a young resident doctor, and you dare butt into the affairs of other attending physicians?” she asked.
Ma Yanlin felt warmth fill his heart. “I’m not young, okay?”

Wei Man felt her whole body heat up with how Ma Yanlin looked at her, and she walked closer to him before she whispered, “I have fewer lessons this week. I can skip one of the lessons and stay at home. You should take a day off work too.”

Ma Yanlin was attracted by how passionate this young lady from Peking Union Medical College Hospital was, and he forgot about the fear of being dominated by her for a period of time. He nodded and hesitantly said, “It’s quite hard to take leave from Doctor Ling’s side.”

“I understand that Doctor Ling doesn’t talk much. Just tell him that you’re taking leave to accompany me.” Wei Man stopped talking for a while before she said, “Today’s accident is a major one. You’re going to be working around the clock for this one, I think. Isn’t it reasonable to take a day off after this is over?”

“Okay... I’ll ask Doctor Zuo about the working schedule first.” Ma Yanlin was a bit excited, nervous, and relieved. If he had to work for one day and one night, it would no longer be a difficult thing for him to be forced to take some medication.
Wei Man wore a satisfied smile and thought, ‘Since my husband’s worked for a whole day, he won’t feel so embarrassed if I give him some medication.’
When Wei Man thought about what would happen after Ma Yanlin took his medication, she felt her entire body go numb.

“Doctor Wei.” A resident doctor from the Department of Urology ran over and gasped for breath. He was late because he had been held back by a patient, so he could only let a second-string attending physician go over there first. However, he still felt bad about it.
“Go and change your attire first. Today’s workload is definitely going to be heavy.” Wei Man’s expression was more serious when she was dealing with junior doctors.
The resident doctor nodded and stared at Ma Yanlin. “I heard that there are a few seriously wounded patients?” he asked.

“Yes,” Ma Yanlin explained the situation again, and after he finished, he said, “This is just the beginning. We still don’t know the situation after this. All of you should make more preparations. Doctor Ling has asked doctors from many departments to come over.”

Wei Man nodded seriously and added, “Based on the current situation, it’s unavoidable that we’ll encounter penile fractures, ureter ruptures, and kidney contusions. Now, go and inform the department to prepare the instrument and consumables. It’s not surprising to have two or three penile fractures in a boiler explosion...”
“Yes...” The resident doctor pushed his thighs together and went to make the call.
Ma Yanlin also pushed his thighs together and found himself 120% in work mode.
All the doctors who joined the emergency consultation were in high spirits and were 120% careful.

Firstly, the boiler explosion could turn into a much more serious accident. Even if it did not, it was still no laughing matter. Regardless of which level it was at, it had to be reported to the State Council. There was no need to even think. In the next two hours, the leaders of Yun Hua City and Changxi Province would come over after one another like a wave. If they were not careful right now, it meant that the doctors were not harsh enough with themselves, and the doctors would not be able to handle their conscience gnawing at them too.
Secondly, this was an emergency consultation issued by Ling Ran.
The doctors from Yun Hua Hospital still felt a little terrified when they needed to deal with Ling Ran.
It was because Ling Ran was not an easygoing doctor who would make an exception for someone. Most importantly, Ling Ran had invaded too many departments.

From the Hand Surgery Department to the Orthopedics Department, then the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery, followed by the General Surgery Department, and now, the Department of Cardiovascular Surgery...

The other departments, which had not been invaded did not know whether Ling Ran already had the ability to invade their departments. No matter what, the doctors all saw and knew that once Ling Ran invaded a department, his surgery skills in that field would be at a high level. No one knew how much time he spent training secretly.
Such doctors were not uncommon in the hospital.

Since ancient times, famous doctors were like outstanding students who studied secretly in the dark. Hence, many academicians and specialists would usually remain quiet, and when they decided to take action, they would achieve the highest level in the field. They would still remain at the top even if they dealt with new and advanced skills.
None of the famous doctors would reveal their learning methods so that others would look at their failures to be amused.

If anyone looked at the resumes and the publicity materials of famous doctors, they would usually be things such as “Completed XXX surgery cases without any mistakes.” If people asked how they achieved that, they would usually mention that they relied on some kind of organization for their success, and they would also say they had a solid foundation.

The doctors in Yun Hua Hospital had no idea what Ling Ran had learned and what level he was at when it came to those skills he was learning. That aside, no one currently wanted to be called out by Ling Ran.
Therefore, many departments sent out their third-string doctors.

In a normal emergency consultation, it would be sufficient to send out first-string doctors from each department. However, when they ran into a major accident, attending physicians would attend the consultation to ensure the surgery scope was within the normal range of their abilities.
However, the number of third-string doctors who attended today far surpassed the normal number that would be there for a consultation.

Zuo Cidian felt proud when he stood beside Ling Ran. As more people came over, he took a step forward and whispered, “Doctor Ling, I see that some doctors haven’t had their meals. Why don’t I ask the cafeteria to prepare some food?”
“Do we have time to have our meals?” Ling Ran looked at Zuo Cidian strangely.

“Not everyone can stand next to the operating table, right?” Zuo Cidian smiled. “I’ll get someone to prepare some cold food. If they can’t prepare it, we can ask some restaurants to send food over. Then anyone can just eat whenever they want to.”
“Hmm, okay then,” Ling Ran agreed after he thought about it.

Even if someone got blown up into pieces, there were still some procedures to be followed whether it was preoperative procedures or postoperative procedures. The doctors could not just rush forward and perform the surgery. Furthermore, there were a limited number of operating theaters, and the area around the operating table was also limited. Hence, they would not be so busy that everyone would not have time to eat.
Zuo Cidian obeyed Ling Ran’s instructions and went away. This meant that he naturally left the role of a first-string doctor so that he would not become a hindrance to Ling Ran’s treatment group.
“Thirty seconds.” The reception nurse raised her voice to inform everyone.

Ling Ran nodded and turned around slightly. He said, “The General Surgery Department will take care of the first two patients in the first ambulance. Perform exploratory laparotomy and communicate with us in time if any problems occur. Remember to update the medical record. Zhang Anmin, you will take care of the male patient in the second ambulance. Again, let us know in time if there is any problem. The female patient is experiencing circulatory failure. Let the Emergency Department perform resuscitation on her first. Doctor Zhou, can you take care of that?”
“Alright,” Doctor Zhou immediately agreed to it. He did not hesitate in obeying orders just because he was considered a senior in rank to Ling Ran in the Emergency Department.
He saw it with his own eyes. Ling Ran had delegated tasks to the General Surgery Department as well as the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery without even asking them about anything.
From Doctor Zhou’s perspective, if Ling Ran could even ask them any questions, that would be him showing his respect.

Ling Ran continued to delegate tasks, and during this period of time, he tried his best to understand the conditions of the patients in the ambulances. Of course, when the patients reached the hospital, he would proceed to check them once more, and if there was any misjudgment, he could still change his orders at the very last minute.
“Third ambulance...
“Fourth ambulance...”
Ling Ran made arrangements for the patients one after another. He did not bother about the preference of each department or the level of the doctors from each department.
Zuo Cidian was worried at first, but later, he had his questions answered.
After all, the ones who attended were obedient. Since the patients’ treatment was their focus, straightforward orders would be more acceptable and easily understood by every doctor.

sentences.text: Wei Man held a suitcase and kept running.
She only stopped to catch her breath when she saw the sign of the Emergency Medical Center ahead of her.
She checked the time and thought, ‘Luckily, I’m not late.’
Since Yun Hua Hospital built the Emergency Medical Center, its requirements for the standards of emergency consultation had also increased.

The requirement for doctors from other departments to arrive at the latest within ten minutes remained unchanged from the past, but now, a requirement for them to arrive within eight minutes had also been added to serve as the first borderline.
If a doctor could reach in eight minutes, good comments would be left in his or her record.
Ten minutes was still considered normal, and anyone who took more than ten minutes to arrive would fail to meet the requirement.

When this procedure was implemented, most of the doctors could reach within eight minutes, thus the borderline of eight minutes had now become the maximum amount of time allowed for doctors to arrive.
No department director would want their record to be worse than the record of others.

However, when the doctors in each department truly had to implement it, the pressure on them inevitably increased largely because the acceptable amount of time they had to reach the Emergency Department had been reduced by two minutes.
This meant that once the doctors received the call, they needed to rush over to the Emergency Medical Center, and they needed to deal with all the obstacles they met on the way quickly.
Wei Man was the attending physician on duty in the Department of Urology today.
She had to explain the situation to the family member of a patient with kidney stones, which was why she was in a bit of a hurry.
As the lift was not efficient, she ran over using the stairs.
Ma Yanlin knew that his wife was the person on duty in the Department of Urology today.
He felt sorry for his wife and waited for her outside.
He immediately waved at her when he saw her.
“I’m not late, right?” Wei Man was still quite serious when she was working.
She spoke in a business-like tone when she saw Ma Yanlin.
“No,” Ma Yanlin quickly replied and lowered his voice to say, “A boiler in the industrial park exploded.
There are six seriously wounded patients being sent over now, and there should still be some other patients as well.”
Wei Man nodded slowly and looked at Ling Ran, who was in the frontmost row.
She subconsciously said, “Thankfully, Doctor Ling is on duty today.”
“I know, right?” Ma Yanlin immediately replied and spoke out of concern for her again, “Are you the only one from your department?
The third-string doctors were informed, right?”
“They were definitely informed.
Associate Chief Physician Guo will come over soon,” Wei Man said in a flirtatious tone and rolled her eyes at Ma Yanlin.
“You’re just a young resident doctor, and you dare butt into the affairs of other attending physicians?” she asked.
Ma Yanlin felt warmth fill his heart.
“I’m not young, okay?”
Wei Man felt her whole body heat up with how Ma Yanlin looked at her, and she walked closer to him before she whispered, “I have fewer lessons this week.
I can skip one of the lessons and stay at home.
You should take a day off work too.”
Ma Yanlin was attracted by how passionate this young lady from Peking Union Medical College Hospital was, and he forgot about the fear of being dominated by her for a period of time.
He nodded and hesitantly said, “It’s quite hard to take leave from Doctor Ling’s side.”
“I understand that Doctor Ling doesn’t talk much.
Just tell him that you’re taking leave to accompany me.” Wei Man stopped talking for a while before she said, “Today’s accident is a major one.
You’re going to be working around the clock for this one, I think.
Isn’t it reasonable to take a day off after this is over?”
“Okay...
I’ll ask Doctor Zuo about the working schedule first.” Ma Yanlin was a bit excited, nervous, and relieved.
If he had to work for one day and one night, it would no longer be a difficult thing for him to be forced to take some medication.
Wei Man wore a satisfied smile and thought, ‘Since my husband’s worked for a whole day, he won’t feel so embarrassed if I give him some medication.’
When Wei Man thought about what would happen after Ma Yanlin took his medication, she felt her entire body go numb.
“Doctor Wei.” A resident doctor from the Department of Urology ran over and gasped for breath.
He was late because he had been held back by a patient, so he could only let a second-string attending physician go over there first.
However, he still felt bad about it.
“Go and change your attire first.
Today’s workload is definitely going to be heavy.” Wei Man’s expression was more serious when she was dealing with junior doctors.
The resident doctor nodded and stared at Ma Yanlin.
“I heard that there are a few seriously wounded patients?” he asked.
“Yes,” Ma Yanlin explained the situation again, and after he finished, he said, “This is just the beginning.
We still don’t know the situation after this.
All of you should make more preparations.
Doctor Ling has asked doctors from many departments to come over.”
Wei Man nodded seriously and added, “Based on the current situation, it’s unavoidable that we’ll encounter penile fractures, ureter ruptures, and kidney contusions.
Now, go and inform the department to prepare the instrument and consumables.
It’s not surprising to have two or three penile fractures in a boiler explosion...”
“Yes...” The resident doctor pushed his thighs together and went to make the call.
Ma Yanlin also pushed his thighs together and found himself 120% in work mode.
All the doctors who joined the emergency consultation were in high spirits and were 120% careful.
Firstly, the boiler explosion could turn into a much more serious accident.
Even if it did not, it was still no laughing matter.
Regardless of which level it was at, it had to be reported to the State Council.
There was no need to even think.
In the next two hours, the leaders of Yun Hua City and Changxi Province would come over after one another like a wave.
If they were not careful right now, it meant that the doctors were not harsh enough with themselves, and the doctors would not be able to handle their conscience gnawing at them too.
Secondly, this was an emergency consultation issued by Ling Ran.
The doctors from Yun Hua Hospital still felt a little terrified when they needed to deal with Ling Ran.
It was because Ling Ran was not an easygoing doctor who would make an exception for someone.
Most importantly, Ling Ran had invaded too many departments.

From the Hand Surgery Department to the Orthopedics Department, then the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery, followed by the General Surgery Department, and now, the Department of Cardiovascular Surgery...
The other departments, which had not been invaded did not know whether Ling Ran already had the ability to invade their departments.
No matter what, the doctors all saw and knew that once Ling Ran invaded a department, his surgery skills in that field would be at a high level.
No one knew how much time he spent training secretly.
Such doctors were not uncommon in the hospital.
Since ancient times, famous doctors were like outstanding students who studied secretly in the dark.
Hence, many academicians and specialists would usually remain quiet, and when they decided to take action, they would achieve the highest level in the field.
They would still remain at the top even if they dealt with new and advanced skills.
None of the famous doctors would reveal their learning methods so that others would look at their failures to be amused.

If anyone looked at the resumes and the publicity materials of famous doctors, they would usually be things such as “Completed XXX surgery cases without any mistakes.” If people asked how they achieved that, they would usually mention that they relied on some kind of organization for their success, and they would also say they had a solid foundation.
The doctors in Yun Hua Hospital had no idea what Ling Ran had learned and what level he was at when it came to those skills he was learning.
That aside, no one currently wanted to be called out by Ling Ran.
Therefore, many departments sent out their third-string doctors.
In a normal emergency consultation, it would be sufficient to send out first-string doctors from each department.
However, when they ran into a major accident, attending physicians would attend the consultation to ensure the surgery scope was within the normal range of their abilities.
However, the number of third-string doctors who attended today far surpassed the normal number that would be there for a consultation.
Zuo Cidian felt proud when he stood beside Ling Ran.
As more people came over, he took a step forward and whispered, “Doctor Ling, I see that some doctors haven’t had their meals.
Why don’t I ask the cafeteria to prepare some food?”
“Do we have time to have our meals?” Ling Ran looked at Zuo Cidian strangely.
“Not everyone can stand next to the operating table, right?” Zuo Cidian smiled.
“I’ll get someone to prepare some cold food.
If they can’t prepare it, we can ask some restaurants to send food over.
Then anyone can just eat whenever they want to.”

Even if someone got blown up into pieces, there were still some procedures to be followed whether it was preoperative procedures or postoperative procedures.
The doctors could not just rush forward and perform the surgery.
Furthermore, there were a limited number of operating theaters, and the area around the operating table was also limited.
Hence, they would not be so busy that everyone would not have time to eat.
Zuo Cidian obeyed Ling Ran’s instructions and went away.
This meant that he naturally left the role of a first-string doctor so that he would not become a hindrance to Ling Ran’s treatment group.

Remember to update the medical record.
Zhang Anmin, you will take care of the male patient in the second ambulance.

The female patient is experiencing circulatory failure.
Let the Emergency Department perform resuscitation on her first.
Doctor Zhou, can you take care of that?”

“Third ambulance...

Ling Ran made arrangements for the patients one after another.
He did not bother about the preference of each department or the level of the doctors from each department.

chapters.title: Chapter 977: Supervisor
paragraphs: The moment the ambulance made a stop, a patient who was practically a mash of flesh and blood was wheeled out.
The paramedic reported quickly with one hand pressed on the patient’s abdomen. “HR 120, BP 120/90, penetrative wound on the abdomen, breathing rate 22, pure oxygen was administered before arrival...”

“Follow me, we’re going straight to the surgical floor.” The attending physician from the General Surgery Department was an experienced one. He only took one glance at the position of the wound and started walking.

On ordinary days, when a patient whose belly was pierced through showed up, the doctor in charge at the General Surgery Department would definitely pay him a lot of attention. The doctor might even ask a chief physician to come over for a consultation.
Not only were most attending physicians worried that they were not capable enough, but they were also unwilling to take up large responsibilities.

However, when everyone realized that what had happened might be an extremely major incident, it was hard for them to pay attention to a patient who was merely suffering from a penetrative wound on his belly.

The attending physician of the General Surgery Department merely glanced at the associate chief physician beside him, who was standing with his hands raised in front of his chest, before bringing the patient to the operating theater right away according to Ling Ran’s arrangements. He immediately performed an exploratory laparotomy, which saved a lot of effort.

Some patients who were sent in after that were transferred to the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery, while the Emergency Department treated those with circulatory shock. Because of this, Ling Ran got to relax a little.
Soon, Zuo Cidian who was done ordering the kitchen staff members to prepare food rushed back to the resuscitation room. He saw that Doctor Zhou was busy barking orders.
Doctor Zhou was busy...
‘What?
‘Old Zhou is busy?’

Zuo Cidian froze for a moment and took a good look at his surroundings. He saw Doctor Zhou, Ma Yanlin, and a few other doctors busy treating patients. He did not see Yu Yuan, but this was very normal given her height. ‘But where’s Doctor Ling?’
Zuo Cidian immediately exited the resuscitation room. He only felt a little more at ease when he saw Ling Ran.

But right after that, Zuo Cidian became anxious again. He quickly walked over to Ling Ran, and he looked like a child who was chasing after Fragrance Yard as he did so. He whispered into Ling Ran’s ear, “Doctor Ling, is everything over here... alright?”
“Everything’s normal,” Ling Ran said.
“Normal, huh...?” Zuo Cidian looked around hesitantly and said in a hushed tone, “I see that the doctors in the other departments are starting to operate on patients already...”
Ling Ran understood what Zuo Cidian meant. He smiled and said, “There had only been four ambulances in total. Let’s wait for a little while.”

“Oh, okay. you’re right. Doctors in those departments have dealt with patients from those ambulances, and we are not the right people to treat the injuries that those patients are suffering from either... I guess we can be considered as reserve forces...” Zuo Cidian articulated what Ling Ran was implying in a dramatic manner. He was standing behind Ling Ran with his body straight and head raised. He faced the reception door, and he wore a solemn expression.
Compared with minor incidents, major incidents were complicated because often, a large number of patients would suddenly be sent in.

If a person were to only consider the kinds of injuries suffered by the wounded, it was not a given that patients who got injured during major incidents would suffer more serious wounds than patients who got injured during minor incidents. However, when a large number of patients were sent in all of a sudden, it would put huge pressure on the medical staff members. It was just like a strong surge of electric current that would penetrate materials that did not have strong enough insulation properties.

Whenever institutions like hospitals were hard hit by this kind of occurrence, total chaos would ensue, and things would be a total mess. When circumstances were extremely dire, doctors would have to categorize patients according to the severity of their injuries and treat the more seriously wounded ones first. This was exactly what Ling Ran did back in Brazil.

Similarly, as long as institutions such as hospitals were not hit hard by an astronomical number of patients, the only difference the number of patients would make would be the degree of fatigue of the doctors.

Take an ordinary tertiary Grade A hospital in China as an example. It was very normal around a hundred surgeries to be performed by various doctors of the hospital every day. And it was impossible for a normal incident to wound a hundred patients. For hospitals, the only part that allowed the doctors to last through this sort of accident was the knowledge that this hardest pressure only happened once in a blue moon.
Ling Ran knew this very well, and Zuo Cidian could understand where Ling Ran was coming from.
Yet, after waiting for a short while, Zuo Cidian became worried again. “Doctor Ling, what if... this is all there is to the incident? The remaining patients might also be sent to other hospitals...”
“Do you have a strong desire to operate on patients today?” Ling Ran looked dumbfoundedly at Zuo Cidian.

Zuo Cidian chuckled. “I’m just putting myself in your shoes. You’ve already let other departments operate on the patients who were sent in. What if no more patients are sent over? If that happens, you wouldn’t get to carry out any surgeries.”
“I’ve already sent the patients to other departments. But this doesn’t mean that I can’t take the patients back from them, right?” Ling Ran turned and glanced at Zuo Cidian.
“Take the patients back?” Zuo Cidian widened his eyes, and he only took a moment to understand what Ling Ran meant. “So, you’re planning to...”
Ling Ran looked at Zuo Cidian with a baffled expression. To him, this was the most natural thing to do.

Zuo Cidian gulped. He racked his brains and took the initiative to come up with an excuse for Ling Ran. “At least... Doctor Zhou would definitely be willing for you to take his position... Wait. So, did Doctor Zhou get a patient with circulatory shock?
Ling Ran looked at Zuo Cidian in bewilderment and asked, “We’ve already received a report from the site of the incident. Two more ambulances will be coming over very soon.”
“Oh...” Zuo Cidian froze for a moment and cleared his throat pretentiously a few times. “Doctor Ling, I’ll definitely work hard to resuscitate the patients who are coming in.”

Ling Ran nodded. He then shook his head and said, “None of the patients who are being sent over suffer from Colles’ fracture. You can treat those who suffer from minor injuries after they’re sent over. The patients in the first ambulance that is coming over later should be handed over to the Neurosurgery Department.”
Zuo Cidian was disappointed for a moment, but he snapped out of it soon. He was a little relieved as he said, “I’ll do as you say.”
“Five minutes.” A nurse came over and reported the time the ambulances would take to arrive.

Ling Ran nodded in acknowledgment. He then said to Zuo Cidian, “Emergency surgeries are more urgent, and the most important thing is to be able to complete them smoothly. If you want to operate on patients, I’ll arrange for you to carry out some scheduled surgeries later on.”
“Oh... okay...” Zuo Cidian quickly agreed. After he turned away from Ling Ran, he felt a surge of dizziness. ‘What have I just agreed to?’
“Doctor Ling... um...” This was when a nurse ran over and said in a hushed tone, “Can you come over to the operating theater to take a look?”
“Where’s the patient and what’s going on?” Ling Ran sounded steady.
“It’s the patient who was sent to Operating Theater 3 just now...”
“The one belonging to the Orthopedics Department?”
The nurse said in a hushed tone, “Yes. The patient is suspected to be suffering from hemorrhage, so we would like you to take a look.”
“Operating theater 3? Who’s inside there right now?” Zuo Cidian asked.
“Attending Physician Liu is the chief surgeon. Associate Chief Physician Yao has also gone over,” the nurse said softly.
“But they haven’t managed to stop the hemorrhage yet?” Zuo Cidian followed up with two questions.
“No,” the nurse answered.
“I’ll go over and take a look.” Ling Ran looked at the clock and started walking.

Zuo Cidian chased after Ling Ran and said in a hushed tone, “Doctor Ling, even Associate Chief Physician Yao is there. It might not be very appropriate for us to go over there now... What if we run into other unexpected circumstances...?”
“We must save lives first before treating illnesses.” Ling Ran did not slow down at all.
Zuo Cidian licked his lips. There was nothing he could say.

After working in the hospital for so long, he had seen a lot of patients who survived and a lot of patients who did not make it. Sometimes, after a person witnessed something repeatedly, he or she would become used to it.
But as Zuo Cidian walked behind Ling Ran, he felt more relaxed, and there was a spring in his steps.
“Doctor Zuo.” Ling Ran turned and called out to him.
“Yes?” Zuo Cidian answered loudly.

“The ambulances will be arriving very soon. Monitor the resuscitation room and order the doctors to resuscitate the patients according to plan. Call me if there’s any problem,” Ling Ran said and left, leaving Zuo Cidian behind.
Zuo Cidian froze for a moment. ‘So, am I considered the on-site supervisor now?’

chapters.title: Chapter 978: Solemn
paragraphs: Ling Ran walked into Operating Theater 3 and saw that the atmosphere there was tense and solemn.

Operating Theater 3 was quite small, and there were more than ten people inside there right now. This could be said to be against the rule, as with so many people inside, sanitization could not be guaranteed.
Given how much the Orthopedics Department placed an emphasis on infection control, this was extremely out of character for them, and this scene should not even appear among them.
However, no one from the Orthopedics Department in the operating theater, from the associate chief physician to the circulating nurse, had any time to care about this.
The doctor was holding a blood bag, the anesthetist looked flustered, and the nurses were walking around in a flurry. All of this silently signaled one thing—chaos had ensued.
Ling Ran said nothing as he put on a mouth face mask. He then walked forward and took a look at the patient.

It was easy to maintain order in the operating theater. A person merely needed to shout loudly for all the people in a flurry to return to a state of order. However, the problem right now did not lie in the medical staff members’ attitude or the protocol. It was more possible that the problem was caused by their skills.

There were more than ten medical staff members inside the operating theater, and none of them knew what to do. Shouting at them would not make them gain superb skills all of a sudden as if they had been blessed by God.
Since they did not know what they should do, no matter how much Ling Ran disciplined them and asked them to act in a proper manner, it would be meaningless.
It was just like how a student would not recover from a cold just because everyone in his class was concerned about him.
Ling Ran decided to focus on the patient first and foremost.

The patient was probably a factory or construction worker. He looked around forty years old, and his face was worn down by years of hard work, typical of those who worked hard for years. His face was deathly pale, and his belly was protruded. There was a bruise on his right leg.

“Six fragments the size of a fingernail had pierced through the patient’s back. We were dealing with that when blood started surging out.” The attending physician did not seem more at ease even though Ling Ran was here. He reported the situation in a flustered manner, and he was not quite able to make things clear.

Associate Chief Physician Yao, the senior doctor who was standing beside Ling Ran, quickly added. “His BP is decreasing rapidly, and we can no longer find the pulse of the dorsal plantar artery of his right leg. I’ve already asked people from the Department of Interventional Services to come over because I’m thinking of doing an angiography for his right leg to determine the bleeding point. But the people there are a little too busy...”
The hospital was obviously hit hard by the massive influx of patients, and they were about to break down.
More than ten medical staff members were trying to treat this patient. These medical staff members could have treated three patients with minor to moderate injuries with no problems.

However, because of how severe the condition of this patient was, the doctors were unable to handle it. They had no choice but to call more and more medical staff members over, including Ling Ran and the people from the Department of Interventional Services.

In the event of Ling Ran not being capable of stopping the hemorrhage or the Department of Interventional Services not being able to produce useful examination results, they would have no choice but to give up on the patient or leave things up to luck.

No matter which choice they decided to go with, it would mean that a life would be lost. It would also mean that more than ten medical staff members worked hard to no avail to save a patient who needed them the most.
Even though Yun Hua Medical Emergency Center was a large institution, when unforeseen circumstances arose, if they were unable to mobilize all their forces, they could easily be defeated.
Ling Ran had participated in many disaster relief efforts before, but his expression still turned solemn.
“The patient is already in severe circulatory shock. With the speed in which he’s losing blood, there’s a huge possibility that his artery is ruptured...” Ling Ran slowly articulated his judgment.
“Yes, I agree with Doctor Ling.” Associate Chief Physician Yao from the Orthopedics Department voiced his agreement.
Right now, he had already lost control of the situation, and he really needed Ling Ran to join them in their efforts.

No matter how things turned out, with another senior doctor working together with them to save the patient, Associate Chief Physician Yao could be relieved of his mental burden as well as responsibility toward the situation.

If Zuo Cidian were here, after hearing the attending physician’s ambiguous words, he would have whipped out his notebook to make some notes. He might even draw a line and state Ling Ran’s scope of responsibility.
However, Ling Ran did not care about all this. He looked at the patient’s abdomen for a moment before shifting his gaze toward the patient’s thigh.

“It’s already too late to perform angiography. All we can do now is to make an emergency judgment.” Ling Ran was not like ordinary doctors, who would think things through again and again until they were extremely certain that they were right before speaking out.

On one hand, it was because the possibilities were endless, and Ling Ran hoped that by saying something, even if it was just a common remark, other doctors could brainstorm together with him and come up with more information. On the other hand, Ling Ran did not care about things like whether he would be held responsible for something or not.

He had always been a person of order, but it was impossible for him to abide by the unspoken rules of society in everything he did. He had basically never been put at a disadvantage when it came to this, so he naturally did not care as much.
Right then, Ling Ran cared the most about increasing the probability of the patient surviving.
He possessed Perfect Level Barehanded Bleeding Control and more than two hundred times of lower limb anatomical dissection experience. Hence, he was confident enough to voice his thoughts.
“Doctor Ling, what should we do now?” Associate Chief Physician Yao from the Orthopedics Department had put more thought into this, and he was stealthily trying to avert responsibility.
Some of the nurses, as well as the anesthetist, managed to read between the lines. They looked at Associate Chief Physician Yao in disdain but did not say anything.
Meanwhile, all the doctors from the Orthopedics Department lowered their heads in unison. They were a little embarrassed but did not dare to say anything about it.

The relationship between high-ranking doctors and their subordinates in the hospital was sometimes even more demanding than how things were like in the military. It was also a greater test. Those who were unable to pass the test would get kicked out sooner or later. It would be very hard for those doctors to survive in a large hospital like Yun Hua Hospital.

Associate Chief Physician Yao was a PhD holder who did his studies full time. He was young and capable, plus he had already become an associate chief physician in the Orthopedics Department even though he was not even forty years old yet. He also led a treatment group. He could be considered a young and successful doctor. No matter how he looked at things, he was unwilling to bear the responsibility that came with this surgery.
Now that Ling Ran was the one giving the orders, he had to bear full responsibility.

The attending physician from the Orthopedics Department was also young, and he could not help but lower his head. He was a little embarrassed by the fact that he so brazenly handed over the responsibility to Ling Ran just to avoid blame. He was also a little worried.

“Make an incision on the abdominal wall.” Even though Ling Ran still had to take the ambulances that would be coming later into consideration, he quickly made an order. This meant that he had taken over the responsibility that came with this surgery.
Associate Chief Physician Yao from the Orthopedics Department did not hesitate. He grabbed a scalpel and was ready to make the incision.
“Wait a moment,” Ling Ran said.
Associate Chief Physician Yao sighed internally. Had Ling Ran regained his senses and decided not to take on this responsibility?

However, this was not the case. Ling Ran said, “When the incision is made on the abdominal wall, a lot of blood would definitely flow out. Nurses, go and get more blood bags. Assistants, get two aspirators ready. As for the anesthetist, can you check the tube...? What’s going to happen next is that the moment the incision is made, I’ll immediately look for the bleeding point. Using the right forceps is very important in this case...”
Ling Ran ordered the medical staff members around in detail. Like what Associate Chief Physician Yao was hoping, he had taken command of the situation.
After Ling Ran spoke, the nurses and assistants, as well as the anesthetists, started moving about in an orderly fashion. The operating theater suddenly looked spacious and orderly.
This was the kind of atmosphere that foreshadowed a successful surgery, and it naturally spread out in the operating theater.

Associate Chief Physician Yao could not help but look at Ling Ran, and he had a realization. ‘Yes. As long as this surgery is successful, he won’t have to deal with bearing the responsibility that comes with this surgery. But...’

chapters.title: Chapter 979: A Sensation That He Never Would Have Missed
paragraphs: Associate Chief Physician Yao gazed at the patient on the operating table with a solemn expression. The scalpel felt so heavy, and he felt like a disloyal married man with four girlfriends who was holding the keys to the first girlfriend’s house.
Every single surgeon was familiar with bleeding control, and as an associate chief physician, Associate Chief Physician Yao did it all the time.
That was exactly why he knew how hard it was to deal with this patient’s hemorrhage.

Of course, it was easy to make an incision on the patient’s abdominal wall. But if he was unable to quickly and accurately find the bleeding point, the patient’s blood would flow out like a broken dam, until all his blood vessels were drained. It would be to the point that the blood would not be able to be replaced quickly enough even if blood was transfused into the veins of both his hands.
Associate Chief Physician Yao knew the feeling of how the success of something would be decided in a split second all too well. The pressure that came with it could kill a person.

He tightened his grip on the scalpel and glanced at Ling Ran. He decided to take a step backward. He said with a soft voice, “Doctor Ling, I’ll be performing laparotomy. Will you be executing bleeding control?”

Ling Ran was renowned in the hospital for his amazing bleeding control skills. As for laparotomy, it was nothing difficult, and it was only about as difficult as opening a door with a key. The decision made after the door was opened was more difficult. It was a matter of where to place his hand or the surgical instrument.
Even though the atmosphere in the operating theater was calm and Ling Ran was confident, Associate Chief Physician Yao would rather play it safe.
However, Ling Ran who was busy making commands had no intention of picking up the baton.
He quickly shook his head regretfully. “A new batch of ambulances will be arriving very soon, so you’ll have to do it.”
“Oh... alright.” There was nothing Associate Chief Physician Yao could do. Ling Ran had a good reason. And more importantly, the patient lying on the operating table belonged to him.
In other words, even though he wanted to avert responsibility, he was unable to do it completely.
“I’ll start performing laparotomy, then.” Associate Chief Physician Yao did not say much. As if he was opening a door, he quickly landed his scalpel on the patient’s abdomen and made an incision.
Compared with how things were before where Ling Ran ordered him to open the patient’s abdominal cavity right away, Ling Ran was doing things differently right now.
Associate Chief Physician Yao thought that it was quite a pity. ‘As expected, Doctor Ling has grown as a person. Unlike before, he’s no longer...’

That was when Ling Ran spoke. “Try your best to keep the incision closer to the crotch area. After slicing open the peritoneum, you can insert your hand into the abdominal cavity and move it to the right. See if you can find the bleeding point. I reckon that it should be thirty degrees from the midline...”
Associate Chief Physician Yao froze for a moment. ‘Such detail!’
However, there was no time for him to ask any questions.
Associate Chief Physician Yao held his breath a little. He started focusing all his attention on the patient the way he used to put his full focus on his exam papers during examinations.

No matter how much a person prepared himself before an examination and no matter what kind of good or bad things he had predicted, the moment he entered the examination hall, he could only depend on himself. And no matter what kind of accident befell him, he would have no choice but to accept it calmly.
It was the same when it came to surgeries.

Before Associate Chief Physician Yao performed the incision, all kinds of thoughts ran through his mind. He tried to avert responsibility and look for help. But right after he started making the incision, all these were in the past.
All had been said and done...
And his performance in the operating theater would decide the final outcome of the surgery.

Associate Chief Physician Yao made an incision with his eyebrows furrowed and ordered his assistants to aspirate. He then did as Ling Ran had said and slowly inserted his hand into the patient’s abdominal cavity.
Associate Chief Physician Yao was neither experienced nor confident when it came to barehanded bleeding control. Hence, he was doing it quite slowly, and he was hesitant throughout the process.
Fortunately, Ling Ran did not say anything about it, and Associate Chief Physician Yao breathed an internal sigh of relief.
It would be embarrassing for him to have Ling Ran point out his flaw.
“Have you found the bleeding point?” Ling Ran’s voice rang out from behind.

“Still looking for it.” Associate Chief Physician Yao continued looking for the bleeding point. ‘There’s so much blood inside, and I can’t see anything. How is it possible for me to find the bleeding point in such a short time?’

Ling Ran furrowed his eyebrows a little. He waved and summoned the Virtual Human. He looked at where Associate Chief Physician Yao’s hand was and made an incision on the Virtual Human. He then dug around the abdominal cavity before dismissing the Virtual Human.

He could only get more time to use the Virtual Human courtesy of Intermediate Treasure Chests, so he tried to minimize its usage as much as possible. On the other hand, he could drink Energy Serums whenever he wanted to.

“Associate Chief Physician Yao, can you position your index finger parallel to your arm and move it forward by 0.3 inches?” Ling Ran told Associate Chief Physician Yao where the bleeding point was according to what he had seen in the Virtual Human’s abdominal cavity.

“Oh... alright.” Associate Chief Physician Yao was not convinced that Ling Ran could determine the position of the bleeding point so correctly from a distance, but he did not stubbornly refuse to follow Ling Ran’s instruction. There was no harm in trying. The patient’s abdominal cavity was full of blood right now anyway, and he could not see a thing.
Associate Chief Physician Yao flexed his index finger a little and looked at Ling Ran.
“Bend it before straightening it.” Ling Ran thought that Associate Chief Physician Yao was asking him about the maneuver.
Associate Chief Physician Yao smiled as he bent and straightened his index finger.
Associate Chief Physician Yao could feel a slight pressure on his fingertip. It was a sensation that he never would have missed.
Associate Chief Physician Yao did not even have time to stop smiling before he quickly applied force using his index finger by straightening it.
“I found it!” Associate Chief Physician Yao gasped. He was kind of pleasantly surprised.
He had always depended on visual observation when it came to barehanded bleeding control. Aside from this, major bleeding points like this were rarely dealt with using barehanded bleeding control.

Associate Chief Physician Yao only had to move his finger a little, and he was able to complete a task that had seemed arduous to him. Right now, he felt like a student who had correctly spotted the questions that came out during an examination. He also felt like a student who saw scribbles that matched the answer to a question perfectly during an examination.
“Make sure that you don’t use too much force.” Ling Ran wore a calm expression. He turned to ask the anesthetist. “Quickly transfuse blood. We have a BP reading?”
“Yes. I’m transfusing blood.” The anesthetist was also in a daze.
He usually assisted in surgeries carried out by doctors from the Orthopedics Department and Associate Chief Physician Yao. He had never heard something like this before, let alone seen it.

It was no news in Yun Hua Hospital that Ling Ran was good at barehanded bleeding control. But when it came to instructing another person on how to find the bleeding point... At least, the anesthetist knew that Associate Chief Physician Yao was not capable of this. He knew this all too well.
The operating theater was rather quiet.
Ling Ran stood quietly and watched as the anesthetist replenished the patient’s fluid and blood...
“If there’s no other problem, I’ll take my leave first.” Unlike usual, Ling Ran did not touch the patient from the beginning to the end. But his state of mind was the same.
Associate Chief Physician Yao turned to glance at the screen so that he did not have to meet eyes with Ling Ran.
He was far from calm right now.

His hand was still soaked in the patient’s blood, and his fingertip was still rested on the patient’s ruptured blood vessel. This was a very normal thing for surgeons. But when he recalled what had just happened, Associate Chief Physician Yao was unable to say anything normal.
*Swish*
Ling Ran nodded and left the operating theater, back to the frontline of the Emergency Medical Center.
Associate Chief Physician Yao lowered his head again and widened the incision. After the aspirators served their purpose, he looked at the bleeding point and started stitching it up.

He was stitching it up very slowly. Not only was it because the ruptured blood vessel was located in a bad position which made things a little difficult, but it was also because he failed to calm himself down.
He could not help but recall what had just happened, and he felt as if someone was asking him if he had just operated on the patient under Ling Ran’s guidance like a resident doctor.

He was stitching it up very slowly.
Not only was it because the ruptured blood vessel was located in a bad position which made things a little difficult, but it was also because he failed to calm himself down.
He could not help but recall what had just happened, and he felt as if someone was asking him if he had just operated on the patient under Ling Ran’s guidance like a resident doctor.

chapters.title: Chapter 980: Bleeding
paragraphs: When Huo Congjun hurried to the hospital from home, the climatic impact from the third wave of ambulances had already died down.

The doctors who were still in the Emergency Department’s main hall and not yet dispatched were only two housemen who had seemingly been picked up from somewhere and three or four young resident doctors who had just run over from their departments.
However, Ling Ran was still standing in the reception area and had yet to enter the resuscitation room or operating theater as he usually would in the past.
Looking at Ling Ran’s tall and straight body, practically all the medical staff, including Huo Congjun, felt inexplicably relieved.

“How many ambulances came?” Huo Congjun’s expression became much more relaxed. The fact that Ling Ran was not on the playing field yet showed that the Emergency Department still possessed its greatest power, and it also showed that Yun Hua’s emergency system had not collapsed.
The feeling was similar to when a general’s armored division had yet to be dispatched into battle. Huo Congjun could not help but feel relieved that he was not too late in his return.
Just as Ling Ran ended a voice call, he heard the question from Huo Congjun. He turned around, smiled, and said, “A total of twelve ambulances and twenty-one patients.”
Huo Congjun was about to move forward when his knee went weak. He almost fell and became the twenty-second patient. “How many batches are they separated into?” he hurriedly asked.
“Three batches,” Ling Ran replied.
Huo Congjun asked, “So in just a short period, three batches of patients have arrived?”
“Yes.”
“These guys...” Huo Congjun thought of another possibility. He frowned and asked, “Are there a lot of lightly injured victims? Since we’re providing food and drinks for the paramedics—”
“Every ambulance basically has one who’s seriously injured,” Ling Ran interrupted Huo Congjun’s estimation.

“That’s more like it.” Huo Congjun’s anger quickly disappeared. For hospitals, the performance appraisal of a lightly injured patient was incomparable to that of a severely injured patient. It was especially so for a patient suffering only from external injuries. Even if he broke an arm, he only needed to get two X-rays, a splint, and a cast.

Seriously wounded patients were a different case, especially those who were so seriously injured that they had to enter the ICU. The number and type of fluid replacements they needed alone could use up the entire stock of a small clinic, forcing them to restock.

As the manager of Yun Hua Emergency Medical Center, Huo Congjun spent all his efforts to get the lounge for paramedics as well as drivers so that they could eat meat and drink tea for free. The idea was to get the paramedics to classify the patients spontaneously before they reached the hospitals. ‘You can send lightly wounded patients anywhere, but seriously wounded patients and our hospital’s doctor have to be sent here.’ These were the words written on the pizza boxes in the lounge for paramedics.
However, Huo Congjun suddenly looked at Ling Ran in doubt. “A dozen seriously injured people have been sorted out properly?”
“Yes, I’ve mainly distributed them to various departments. There is one operating theater left. I didn’t let anyone use it,” Ling Ran answered quickly.

Huo Congjun nodded slowly. In such an emergency, the Emergency Medical Center can only carry out the initial treatment, stabilize the patient’s condition, and refer them to another department. Their tasks would then be completed, nonetheless...
Nonetheless...
Huo Congjun was full of doubts as he looked at Ling Ran. He did not even know how he should start asking questions.

“The departments were particularly cooperative. Doctor Ling’s allocation of patients was also reasonable, so the referral went particularly smoothly.” Zuo Cidian slipped out of the corner. He knew about Huo Congjun’s doubts too because Huo Congjun was not the only one who had questions. Other people and Zuo Cidian himself had similar questions.

“Even if the departments cooperated...” Huo Congjun frowned. If he had to pinpoint a certain time when other departments did not cooperate during another emergency of that scale... he would be able to. Of course, there would always be a department or a doctor that would not follow the Emergency Department’s request for various reasons. However, such a degree of incoordination was not necessarily wrong, and it may not even reduce the treatment quality and efficiency.

At the end of the day, each surgeon’s operation method was unique. Even if the hospital’s treatment procedures had turned into streamlined procedures and were so detail-oriented that they could tend to different patients, the patients were always different in the end. The hospital may want to standardize things and streamline procedures a little more, but before the human body could be assembled in a streamlined procedure, the hospital could not be so wilful.

When it came to emergency treatments, different departments and doctors had different habits as well as requirements. All this while, the Emergency Department was never able to get what they asked for fully.
Huo Congjun naturally looked to Zuo Cidian.

Zuo Cidian understood Huo Congjun’s look, just like a cub who understood a lion’s expression. He obediently stretched out his furry paws to let the lion caress it and broke into a cute smile as he said, “How should I say this? Ling Ran’s efficiency in guiding operations is beyond normal levels.”
“Isn’t it typical for him to go beyond the normal level?” Huo Congjun said something which was difficult for others to understand, but standard for Yun Hua Hospital’s staff.
“You should see how Ling Ran guides surgeries.” The Department of Urology’s Associate Chief Physician Guo Liqing walked over slowly.
“He didn’t affect you, did he?” Huo Congjun laughed first.
“No, he didn’t.” Guo Liqing waved his hand and said, “We do accept guidance. Even if we’re affected, it’d be a good influence...”
Huo Congjun heard a slight resentful tone in his voice, but he did not care about it because he also heard the helplessness in Guo Liqing’s voice.
Being helpless in the current environment was not considered a bad thing.
“How did you guide them?” Huo Congjun finally asked Ling Ran what he was concerned about and looked at him.
Ling Ran recalled and said, “I proposed some solutions. Some have been adopted by everyone, and that’s it.”
Huo Congjun continued to look at Guo Liqing.
Guo Liqing could not stop himself from being a little stunned. It was as if he was stuck in some kind of memory.

“Department Director Guo?” Huo Congjun knew that Guo Liqing was a bit strange. Although his level of strangeness was not on par with Ling Ran’s, he was not easy to deal with as well. This was especially so when he waited in the toilet for several days to get clients to undergo circumcision in order to fulfill his oath. In order to make up the count, he even circumcised his own p*nis, and he could be regarded as an example of someone who would definitely fulfill his promises.

“Ling Ran’s eyes are almost as fast as an MRI.” Guo Liqing stopped talking for a while and said, “He is very good at looking at MRI scans. Without an MRI scan, he can still see where the ureter is ruptured. This is the first time I’ve seen such an ability after all the years I’ve lived, I swear.”
“Well...”
Huo Congjun was still putting together all the bits and pieces of information in his mind when two ambulances stopped outside the reception hall’s door.
“Just watch.” Guo Liqing gestured by raising his chin at Huo Congjun.
Right then, two remaining resident doctors and two interns had already rushed over.
Ling Ran was still standing in the reception hall and did not go up immediately to receive the ambulance.

The two resident doctors quickly classified the patients according to the severity of their injuries. The three patients with minor injuries were sent to the treatment room by the interns for further classification and treatment.
The two seriously injured patients passed the place where Ling Ran stood and were pushed all the way into the resuscitation room.
“Wait here, please consult the Cardiothoracic Department.” Ling Ran performed a simple physical examination on the patients one by one before he intercepted one of them.
The other patient was pushed directly into the room, his treatment process unaffected.
Ling Ran told the resident doctor, “Please ask the Cardiothoracic Department to pay attention and observe the intercostal blood vessels. There should be active bleeding.”
He was actually quite certain with his assessment because he had done an ultra-fast dissection using the Virtual Human when the patients passed by him.

It was a trick Ling Ran discovered today. In a very short time, such as in about one second, he dissected the patient horizontally and vertically, which were the coronal plane and vertical plane commonly known in anatomy. So, he could naturally obtain a large amount of information.
If it had been a normal day, it would naturally be a waste for him to use the Virtual Human like that. But in today’s sudden situation, Ling Ran managed to save up a lot of time because of it.
With the time he saved, he could automatically do a lot more things.
Guo Liqing pouted and said to Huo Congjun, “Do you see it now? There’s no need to even do a scan. Just by glancing at the patient, he can directly point out the bleeding point.”
Huo Congjun looked at Guo Liqing like he was a fool. “What’s so difficult about doing that?”
“The Emergency Medical Center can do that now as well?”
Huo Congjun sighed. “I mean, the patient’s chest is still bleeding.”

chapters.title: Chapter 981: Play Around
paragraphs: “Doctor Ling, please explain things to Department Director Huo.” Guo Liqing looked at the patient with the bleeding chest and felt that his trustworthiness just took a hit. That was the quality he valued the most.
Guo Liqing was eager to prove how trustworthy he was.
Ling Ran looked over strangely and asked, “Explain which aspect?”

“Explain how you pointed out the location of the trauma when you consulted other departments, especially in the cases where you accurately pointed out the bleeding point...” Guo Liqing spoke a little vaguely for a period of time.
Ling Ran frowned slightly and said, “Was the explanation just now not clear enough?”

Guo Liqing thought to himself. ‘You didn’t go into detail at all with what you just said.’ But before he spoke again, Guo Liqing could not help but stop to ponder, and he suddenly felt that if he said that, he would be digging his own grave.
“I mean, how did you see the patient’s bleeding point? And by that, I’m saying, how did you see where they were bleeding inside,” Guo Liqing asked a new question.

“It’s a relatively complicated call.” Ling Ran pondered. It was indeed very complicated. Even if he dissected the patient according to the vertical plane and coronal plane, or in more layman terms, even if he cut up the patient in the shape of a cross, he still needed to take a lot into consideration before he was able to find the bleeding point.

Forget everything else, he needed a large accumulation of knowledge in terms of anatomy before he could do that. If Ling Ran did not have more than two hundred abdominal anatomical dissection experiences, more than three thousand upper limb anatomical dissection experiences, more than forty chest anatomical dissection experiences, and twenty brain anatomical dissection experiences... he would not have been able to make a quick judgment on a patient’s condition based on their vertical plane and coronal plane.

In fact, there were already very few doctors who could perform at least ten dissections, much less those who could perform specialized and regional anatomy dissections. The reason was that cadavers were not only difficult to find, but dissection was also very time-consuming. Regional medical anatomy, in particular, consumed more time and energy.

Based on Ling Ran’s understanding of Associate Chief Physician Guo Liqing from the hospital’s Department of Urology, even if he was given a Virtual Human, he would not be able to make such a quick judgment.
In other words, for Associate Chief Physician Guo Liqing, Ling Ran made a complicated judgment.
Ling Ran was sincere when he spoke.
Director Guo Liqing could not help covering his chest. He spoke in such a sincere tone, but it was like a long sharp knife that penetrated his anal pecten, anal valve, and anal sinus...
Guo Liqing stood up straight and wore a calm smile on his face.

As the saying went, “One has to acknowledge his own mistakes, and one has to be calm even when inflicted with One Thousand Years of Pain [1].” When a person tightened his sphincter violently, his face would show a smile that was calm, depressed, had no implications whatsoever, but was still full of emotions.

“Doctor Ling, the paramedics are asking if we can still accept more patients. There’s an ambulance now with two seriously injured patients. They hope to come to Yun Hua Hospital for medical treatment.” The nurse at the reception walked over with brisk steps. She was ladylike and elegant as she arrived quickly to ask this question.
Ling Ran looked at Huo Congjun.

According to the hospital’s “command hierarchy”, when Huo Congjun, the department director of Yun Hua Emergency Medical Center arrived, Ling Ran would naturally need to give up his power to issue instructions, which was different from when he was in the operating theater.

In the operating theater, the chief surgeon was theoretically the king and did not have to give way to anyone. Of course, it was only in theory. Under normal circumstances, junior doctors could never be tougher than senior doctors.
Huo Congjun smiled. “Since you’re doing well in instructing the doctors, continue instructing them. Well, if you want to perform surgery, I’ll issue the commands.”
If Huo Congjun had said those same words to other people, they would have very likely been taken aback or think that Huo Congjun actually meant the opposite.

However, Huo Congjun obviously did not need to use any rhetoric with Ling Ran. When he added the last sentence, he sounded more amiable, and he also sounded like he showed consideration to the whole situation.
Guo Liqing just watched quietly.
There was no way the paramedics were sending another severely wounded patient with a bleeding external wound over.
Guo Liqing still wanted to explore Ling Ran’s bleeding control technique.
Surgeons were never short of curiosity, but most of the surgeons in China were buried under a whole load of tasks.
In the past, Ling Ran’s barehanded bleeding control only made Guo Liqing curious, but Ling Ran’s performance today exceeded Guo Liqing’s expectations.
If he could, he wanted to learn.
Guo Liqing did not speak as he stood beside Ling Ran and waited for the patients to arrive.
Huo Congjun took a glance at Guo Liqing, and he could already guess his thoughts. He also stood next to him quietly and showed no intention of stopping him or asking any questions.
Ling Ran did not even care.
In a moment, the patient was sent over.
“He’s been crushed...” Guo Liqing leaned forward and immediately figured out what was going on. His eyes also immediately fell on Ling Ran because he wanted to see how he would handle it.
Ling Ran furrowed his eyebrows slightly, and he gently waved his fingers in the air.
“Please ask the Orthopedics Department to provide consultation.” Ling Ran turned his head and ordered.
Guo Liqing snorted internally before he whispered to Huo Congjun, “Department Director Huo, when the next patient comes, watch carefully.”
“Yes, I’m watching.” Huo Congjun’s voice was also so low that it sounded as if his vocal cords were in his stomach.
The resident doctor sent by the Orthopedics Department came running like the wind. He reported for duty to Ling Ran and Huo Congjun before he nervously examined the patient on the bed.

He had to do it in front of Ling Ran, Huo Congjun, and an associate chief physician from the Department of Urology. The resident doctor from the Orthopedics Department felt that all his bones had become stiff and were now refusing to move freely.
“By the looks of it, the patient needs to be sent directly to the operating theater, maybe...?” The resident doctor looked at Ling Ran and whispered.
Ling Ran nodded and asked, “Do you still have an empty operating theater?”

The surgical floor’s only purpose was to gather all operating theaters together to save resources. During actual operations, the surgical floor was also used by various departments. Although the Orthopedics department was a powerful department in Yun Hua Hospital and there were many operating theaters allocated for them, most of their patients suffered from orthopedics injuries in the current accident. They were definitely running short of operating theaters.

In fact, as far as Ling Ran’s judgment was concerned, the Orthopedics Department still could not make room at that time, and if they wanted to operate on the patient, they would have to fight for a communal operating theater.
The resident doctor from the Orthopedics Department was baffled by the question. He hesitated for a few seconds. “Shall I call and ask, then?”

“Ask. If it’s not enough, let them apply for a mobile operating theater quickly,” Ling Ran replied. He then put on his gloves again and gave the patient a physical examination. He tried not to touch the wound.
After a while, the patient was pushed away, and the other patients were sent over.
However, there were still no patients with internal bleeding and no bleeding spots that were hidden from view.
Huo Congjun looked at Guo Liqing. “What do you want me to see?”
“Ling Ran ...” Guo Liqing held his breath. “There’s just no way his operating methods were handed to him on a silver platter.”
“You don’t know anything about genii.” Huo Congjun smiled and shook his head.
“All in all, When Ling Ran pointed out where the patients were bleeding just now to the other departments, it was incredible,” Guo Liqing insisted.
Huo Congjun sighed heavily. “Old Guo, the Department of Urology can’t just circumcise patients all day long to earn income. You’ll start hallucinating if you cut too much of the same thing.”
“I swear.” Guo Liqing continued to fight for his reputation.

Huo Congjun raised his eyebrows, but he seemed to be unmoved. However, in his heart, he was weighing the pros and cons. ‘Guo Liqing seems to be quite fun to play with. Should I toy with him a little?’
