chapters.title: Chapter 988: This Pie is Too Large
paragraphs: The occluder was inserted into the patient’s body via a special long delivery sheath before it expanded, just like a parachute being forced to open inside the heart.

The difference was that the occluder was in the shape of dumbbells, and its waist in the middle could fit perfectly at the defect at the left and right atria. Both sides had disks, and the size was different between occluders, and the surgeon could choose the size. The small left disk was only 0.6 inch or 0.7 inch, while the big disk was 2.0 inches or 2.1 inches.
When such a big foreign body was put into a heart, there would naturally be some potential complications. However, for patients who already had severe symptoms, this was an easier plan.

If no intervention surgery was performed, then the person must receive open-heart surgery and sternal closure. In this way, there would be no foreign body in the thoracic cavity, and the issue of rejection could be exempted, but the side effects of open-heart surgery were more severe than those in intervention surgery.

Meanwhile, the room for error in interventional surgeries was far more severe. A good doctor naturally benefited the patient more, but sometimes, the choice of a doctor may not always be more important than the choice of the occluder. Most of the time, there might be a compatible relationship between the occluder and the patient. Some patients would get better with Occluder A, while some were better with Occluder B...
In this case, the interventional surgery by the Cardiology Department and the surgery in the Department of Cardiovascular Surgery became two different things.
The Department of Cardiovascular Surgery tested the doctor’s skills more, while the Cardiology Department allowed the pharmaceutical sales company to show their value.

From a doctor’s perspective, Ling Ran preferred the operation method by the Department of Cardiovascular Surgery. Even though he completed the process of using the occluder to block the defect very smoothly, the accumulation of the sense of accomplishment was not much.
Ling Ran sighed lightly, and his fingers gently fiddled with the device twice before he announced the end of the surgery.
It was not fun at all!

Similar to a laparoscopic surgery, the complexity of an interventional surgery was mainly shown in two ways. One, the surgery required a high degree of meticulousness. Two, the differences and similarities between the three-dimensional reality and the two-dimensional image on the screen were slightly bothersome, especially for newbies. They needed to practice their hand-eye coordination again before they could get used to it.

However, it was a piece of cake for Ling Ran to perform a surgery like this. Forget about the fact that his Perfect Level Atrial Septal Defect Closure could already solve the problem, even without it, his other relevant skills were also sufficient for technical support.
The previous cardiac trauma repair had allowed Ling Ran to touch the heart, hence the interventional surgery today was not novel at all.
Ling Ran shook his head slightly.
Doctor Lai looked at Ling Ran warily.
In his eyes, Ling Ran’s surgery had been performed really well.

In less than fifteen minutes, the surgery was over. A department director would be able to finish the surgery within this amount of time. Therefore, why did Ling Ran sigh? Why did he shake his head? Was he not happy with the Cardiology Department? Was he not happy with the surgery? Or was he not satisfied with the doctors? The surgery had ended, did he still want to get back at them?
Doctor Lai became more worried the more he thought about it, and he broke out in sweat.
“Should I leave the patient in the Cardiology Department?” Ling Ran deliberately asked.

He came to the Cardiology Department because the hospital beds in the Emergency Medical Center were not enough. Naturally, even if the hospital beds were sufficient, Ling Ran would still be willing to look for extra hospital beds.
Department Director Yuan naturally agreed, and he said, “Pass the patient to us. We generally prescribe 10 units of heparin for three days, twice a day.”

“Sure.” Ling Ran also did not want to adjust the operation mode in the Cardiology Department. Nursing care was a completely different branch, and it also required accumulation of experience. Meanwhile, Ling Ran had temporarily lost a bit of his interest in the Cardiology Department.
Doctor Lai’s eyes continued sparkling brightly.
The calmer Ling Ran was, the more he doubted.

After all, this was a surgery from the Cardiology Department. A domestic occluder cost 20,000 to 30,000 RMB, and the imported one would cost 10,000 RMB more, and an interventional surgery generally only took half an hour to finish.
Very few people would let go of a surgery like this that provided such benefits.
Doctor Lai lowered his head. He counted secretly and waited for Ling Ran to speak.
*Shick*
The door of the operating theater opened.
*Shick*
The door of the operating theater was closed.
Doctor Lai raised his head again, and he saw that Ling Ran and his team members had all left the operating theater.
“What’s going on?” Doctor Lai opened his eyes wide, and he felt goosebumps all over his skin.
“Finally, they’re gone.” Department Director Yuan sighed in relief, and he finally put a smile on his face.
“We don’t know what they’re going to do later, though” Doctor Lai’s voice was slightly gloomy.
Department Director Yuan smiled. “We’ll get through one day after another. Don’t think too much about it. At worst, we’ll just let them have all the emergency patients.”
Doctor Lai hurriedly said, “No way. You can’t be soft now. It’s too easy to let go of the patients, and they will definitely demand even more when you start letting go.”
When he heard this, Department Director Yuan subconsciously hesitated.

Giving out the emergency patients was something he thought of for a long time. Naturally, if possible, he was also not willing to give away any patient. The interventional surgery of the Cardiology Department was very quick, so even if they received all patients who fulfilled the indications, they were enough for two to three doctors to operate at full capacity. There were many doctors in the department, so the remaining cases still needed to be passed to the other doctors.
Besides, if they let go of the emergency patients, the conflict within the Cardiology Department would become even more complicated.
Doctors who used to earn 100,000 RMB every month would not think 30,000 RMB to 40,000 RMB was a high income.
However, the skills shown by Ling Ran today made it hard for Department Director Yuan to make his decision.

Nobody had inborn skills. If Ling Ran could develop this kind of skills, then it meant that he had either been scheming against the Cardiology Department for a long time, or he had been planning to get into interventional surgery since a long time ago.
He had paid such a big price for it, so there was no way the Cardiology Department could get away from it easily.

Meanwhile, Doctor Lai murmured, “Department Director, I think we should be as tense about the situation as possible. Forget everything else, the full set of instruments and equipment for the Cardiology Department costs quite a lot of money. If the Emergency Medical Center bought it to compete with us, even if they earn some money, they would still complain about the money they spent secretly. If we’re more unyielding toward the situation and butter up to the leaders a little more, we will still stand a chance...”

“You don’t understand. The independence of the Emergency Medical Center now is very strong.” Department Director Yuan sighed and said, “Based on Ling Ran ‘s current development, the leaders of the hospital will want to keep him in their hands forever. A few hospital directors are only afraid that Ling Ran will feel unhappy and the Emergency Medical Center has other plans. If they are willing to spend money, develop new surgical methods, and perform new projects, as long as they stay in Yun Hua Hospital, no one will disagree to it...”

Department Director Yuan looked intensely at Doctor Lai and said, “You saw Ling Ran’s skills today. If he is not ready to purchase these equipment, then wouldn’t he have practiced in vain over the past few days?”
Doctor Lai could not help but become stunned. “So, is he definitely going to invade us?”

“Yes. So, why don’t we cut this surgery off cleanly as early as possible. After all, if the Emergency Department doesn’t refer the patients to us, we can’t perform the surgery. So, we’ll just pass all the emergency patients to them, and we’ll focus on consultations. We’ll see how it goes from there.” When Department Director Yuan talked about it, he also sighed, “This pie that we hold is way too huge, I suppose.”

He had paid such a big price for it, so there was no way the Cardiology Department could get away from it easily.
Meanwhile, Doctor Lai murmured, “Department Director, I think we should be as tense about the situation as possible.
Forget everything else, the full set of instruments and equipment for the Cardiology Department costs quite a lot of money.
If the Emergency Medical Center bought it to compete with us, even if they earn some money, they would still complain about the money they spent secretly.
If we’re more unyielding toward the situation and butter up to the leaders a little more, we will still stand a chance...”
“You don’t understand.

The independence of the Emergency Medical Center now is very strong.” Department Director Yuan sighed and said, “Based on Ling Ran ‘s current development, the leaders of the hospital will want to keep him in their hands forever.
A few hospital directors are only afraid that Ling Ran will feel unhappy and the Emergency Medical Center has other plans.
If they are willing to spend money, develop new surgical methods, and perform new projects, as long as they stay in Yun Hua Hospital, no one will disagree to it...”
Department Director Yuan looked intensely at Doctor Lai and said, “You saw Ling Ran’s skills today.
If he is not ready to purchase these equipment, then wouldn’t he have practiced in vain over the past few days?”
Doctor Lai could not help but become stunned.
“So, is he definitely going to invade us?”
“Yes.
So, why don’t we cut this surgery off cleanly as early as possible.
After all, if the Emergency Department doesn’t refer the patients to us, we can’t perform the surgery.
So, we’ll just pass all the emergency patients to them, and we’ll focus on consultations.
We’ll see how it goes from there.” When Department Director Yuan talked about it, he also sighed, “This pie that we hold is way too huge, I suppose.”

chapters.title: Chapter 989: Fragrance
paragraphs: When Ling Ran left the operating theater, he received the “mission accomplished” notification from the system.
The reward that he got was a Basic Treasure Chest, which meant that today’s surgery was not perfect.
Ling Ran’s mind began racing, because he had Perfect Level Atrial Septal Defect Closure, yet he could not perform a perfect surgery.
If anyone else were in his place, it would be unreasonable for them to even dream about conducting a perfect interventional cardiovascular surgery on their first try.
However, Ling Ran never took the word “reasonable” for granted.

Perfect level skills resulting in perfect level surgeries were natural, and of course, this being his first interventional cardiovascular surgery was part of the reason why it was not perfect. But what was the reason for him not being able to create a perfect surgery from the perspective of skills?
Ling Ran walked into the shower room, got undressed, and bathed in hot water. While he thought, he did finger stretching exercises.
He exercised by putting his hands together and his fingertips against each other. Then, he pushed his fingers against each other.

The hot water was very comfortable, and Ling Ran intentionally increased the intensity of the exercise. This was the basic training he often did, which could exercise the strength of his fingers to ensure the accuracy and strength in surgeries.
When there was no definite training direction, Ling Ran habitually practiced his basics.
Perhaps, if he strengthened his basics, he could improve his maneuvers in the details of the surgery?
Ling Ran carried on with the exercise with uncertainty.
Since he was free, before he had any ideas, he would naturally exercise his basic skills.
“I heard that Ling Ran went to the Cardiology Department for surgery today.” In the shower room, two more doctors came in and chatted as they walked.

The Emergency Medical Center could provide Ling Ran with a separate room, but the shower room of the surgical suite was public, and the area at the inside was separated into small rooms. The doctors changed clothes in the outer room, and the process was similar to that of a bathhouse. The privacy and decoration in this shower room were slightly better, and it was also more convenient than a public bathhouse. However, the doctors who needed to perform surgeries at the surgical floor could not enjoy things like a private shower room.
Ling Ran, who was in the middle of bathing, paused for a moment when he heard his name. He then continued bathing without paying too much attention to the conversation.
Being talked about was normal for him. He had long been indifferent to the content or people who were involved in such discussions.
The two doctors who had just entered the door were discussing excitedly.
“I have no idea when Ling Ran trained to perform interventional surgeries.”
“Interventional surgeries have always been simple...”
“Are they really that simple?”
Both of them laughed out loud.
“Seriously, have you seen Ling Ran do interventional surgeries?”
After a few seconds of silence, there was a sound of water splashing, and a muffled voice rose. “I’ve seen him do hepatectomy and Achilles tendon repair.”
“Who hasn’t?”
“What do you think about it?”
This time, the water in the bathroom next door splashed, and a faint voice echoed, “It feels good when I watch it, but after I finish watching it, I feel gloomy.”
“Haha, I felt the same, but cardiology surgeries really make a lot of money.”
“That’s why there are competitions for it.”
“Perhaps we’ll get to see something major happening.”
Ling Ran wrapped a bath towel around himself and walked out of the shower room. He was still doing the finger stretching exercises. He turned a deaf ear to the comments of two junior doctors.
He never paid attention to whether the Cardiology Department made a lot of money.

In terms of making money alone, Ling Ran made enough money by being a freelance surgeon on weekends. In addition, when he performed freelance surgeries, the patients would end up staying in those hospitals and not take up his hospital beds in Yun Hua Hospital, which meant that he was also increasing the number of hospital beds he had in that hospital or that department in a disguised manner. For Ling Ran, it was extremely convenient.

The money the Cardiology Department earned was from the consumables. To some extent, they exploited the loophole of the current management system. In terms of the income of a department, it was not really that outstanding.
In other words, the Cardiology Department only had the money and the way to issue more bonuses to the doctors but had no outstanding advantage in purchasing instruments and equipment.
In addition, the surgery they performed in the department was relatively boring, and Ling Ran’s interest in it had been greatly diminished.
The Department of Internal Medicine, at the end, was still the Department of Internal Medicine. Even if they used interventional surgeries, the level was still very low (read: not as fun).
With a department like this, even if Ling Ran was in charge of it, he would leave it for other people to manage it.
He would not compete for it.
Of course, if Department Director Yuan and others insist on having Ling Ran take over the department, Ling Ran would not strongly refuse it.
With that thought, Ling Ran drove home and texted Tian Qi. [The surgery went well and the occluder worked well.]
After a few minutes, Ling Ran got a reply.
[That’s great! What’s for lunch?]
[Meat!] Ling Ran replied just as quickly.
Even though Ling Ran drank an Energy Serum, after spending a whole day in the hospital, he still became hungry, especially after he took a bath.
If Ling Ran could choose, he could eat a pot of meat now.
After he reached home, he parked his car and entered the restaurant. Ling Ran saw a table full of meat and four beautiful copper pots.

Tian Qi was dressed beautifully, she was sitting on the side facing the door. Ling Jiezhou and Tao Ping were sitting on the opposite side, they were talking and laughing. There were two chefs with toques busy preparing the seasonings in the middle.
“Ling Ran, you’re back.” Tian Qi saw Ling Ran immediately, and she smiled so much that her eyes curled up.
“You haven’t eaten?” Ling Ran looked at the time and sat next to Tian Qi. That was the only empty chair left.
Tian Qi nodded vigorously and said, “After you went for surgeries, I took the opportunity to call the board of directors. Once I’m free, I went over to drink some tea with your mother.”
Tao Ping smiled warmly and said, “Tian Qi brought a thirty-year-old Yiwu tea over. It’s very tasty.”
Tian Qi smiled again. “Madam, you gave me a teacup made by a master. It’s also very beautiful.”
“I am glad you like it. Hmm... sit down and have a meal. Now that you’re a busy man, you don’t come back home that often...” Tao Ping said.
Lin Jiezhou coughed a couple of times and said, “I’ll help pour the water.”
Ling Ran had been focusing on the table in front of him.
“I’ve had someone prepare lamb, beef, fish, and vegetables.” Tian Qi introduced the food with a smile and gave Ling Ran a plate of seasoning.
“Hmm... can you please add a little more pepper?” Ling Ran pointed at the middle of the seasoning.
“Oh, you like chili?” Tian Qi was extremely surprised.
Ling Ran nodded. “Most of the time. Why do you ask?”
“I thought that handsome people would not eat chili,” Tian Qi said in a surprised manner.
Once she finished speaking, Tian Qi quickly tried to cover up what she said, “By the way, has the sponsor given you the funds for the Emergency Medical Center to build the ICU? Do you need our help?”
“I don’t know.” Ling Ran shrugged. “Department Director Huo said that we’ll be able to start using it in two months.”
“After the construction, there will be a lot of follow-up work. If you need help, you can come to us,” Tian Qi said as she took mutton and put it in Ling Ran’s pot.
The water boiled, and slowly, its aroma floated in the air.

chapters.title: Chapter 990: Increase
paragraphs: “Doctor Miao, we’ll be counting on you this time.” The patient’s family showed courtesy and respect on their faces.

Miao Tansheng answered with great ease before he smiled and said, “President Pei, don’t worry. I will make proper arrangements for you later. Your family doesn’t need to feel too burdened with this. Just make some preparations and be admitted into the clinic on time. If any family member is willing to keep her accompanied, we have a single room. If it’s not convenient for you to keep her company, we also have a nurse to take care of her for twenty-four hours of the day. So, please rest assured.”
“A single room? Your clinic... I don’t think it looks very big. Should we stay in Yun Hua Hospital?”

“Then, she will be the patient in Yun Hua Hospital. Doctor Ling will also perform consultations in Yun Hua Hospital every week.” Miao Tansheng smiled faintly. Ling Ran gave out his consultation slots according to his surgical volume now, so it was not easy to get a number in Yun Hua Hospital.
President Pei fell silent for a few seconds before he said, “Money is not the problem. Which side has better conditions?”

“We’ve rented a room at the residential building next to us. After the renovation, we added new furniture. It’s not very luxurious, but it has a very homey feel, so it’ll be more comfortable than staying in the inpatient ward for senior cadres in the hospital.” Miao Tansheng smiled faintly, because all these were done by him.

“Alright. Actually, we don’t really care about who is accompanying her and who her caregiver is. We mainly hope that the surgery can be done smoothly and that we can get a good outcome.” President Pei sounded serious.

Miao Tansheng smiled and said, “President Pei, we’ve talked about this before. Your daughter’s surgery will be performed by Doctor Ling, and Lower Groove Clinic is also one of the designated hospitals registered under Doctor Ling’s multi-sited license. When it comes to nursing care, especially in regards to recovery, we have experienced nurses and doctors as well as staff recruited from Yun Hua Hospital. But whether the outcome is satisfactory or not will be a very subjective issue.”

President Pei stared at Miao Tansheng, and he only grunted after a long while. Then, he sighed again, “My daughter has been learning dancing for ten years, so she can’t give it up just because of an injury.”

Miao Tansheng whispered, “I understand your feelings. I truly understand. Since Lower Groove Clinic developed this program, many patients who come to us are like your daughter. Some like to play sports, some like to dance, but they were all unfortunately injured. Many patients with better financial conditions have looked around before they finally approached us, and all they hoped was to get the best treatment. Meanwhile, we will not just rest on our laurels. We will try our best to treat your daughter...”
Miao Tansheng had been working in the field of cosmetic surgery for a few years, so his oratory skills had improved without his knowledge.

Although he sounded slightly like a salesman, the words he chose sounded nice, and he also catered to their wishes. So when President Pei and his wife listened to him, their facial expressions slowly became relieved.
At this time, President Pei’s wife sat up straight, and she said, “Doctor Miao, I want to ask an unprofessional question. If I’m wrong, please don’t feel unhappy.”

“No worries, please say.” Miao Tansheng’s mood was extremely good. He performed both cosmetic surgeries and the Achilles tendon repair in a private clinic, but when he performed cosmetic surgeries, while the patients and their families were not too arrogant, they still behaved as if they were superior to him, and they had the mindset that if they paid, they were obliged to good service. However, since the clinic launched the Achilles tendon repair programme, the patients and their families that Miao Tansheng met were delightful. They were humble, friendly, and polite, and they looked exactly like how a patient should be when they sought medical advice from the doctor’s perspective.
Miao Tansheng needed this kind of respect the most, especially when he has been expelled from the healthcare system and was on his own.

President Pei’s wife politely said, “Doctor Miao, I heard that the Achilles tendon repair performed by Doctor Ling will leave a big scar. In this case, can you come up with any solution? You know, my daughter is just sixteen years old. In the future... if there’s a scar on her leg in the future, it’ll be very ugly.”
Miao Tansheng understood and nodded. He slowly said, “In this case, do you want to reconsider minimally invasive surgery?”
“If we choose minimally invasive surgery, she will not be able to dance again, right?” President Pei’s wife said uneasily.

Miao Tansheng hesitated for a few seconds before he said, “There are also cases of people recovering from minimally invasive surgery. Besides, your daughter is still very young, so her recovery will be better. But if we talk only about the strength of the Achilles tendon, then the effects from open surgery are definitely the best. You need to judge this on your own.”
“All the athletes received open Achilles tendon repair, right?” President Pei asked by the side. He had done some investigations and preparations, or else, he would not look for Lower Groove Clinic.
President Pei’s wife glared at her husband, then she turned around and said, “Doctor Miao, how about this? Please ask Doctor Ling to make a smaller incision, and try to make the sutures tighter—”

“This depends on the situation.” Miao Tansheng dared not agree to this kind of request, so he answered evasively, “I’ll suggest to Doctor Ling to make the incision smaller to a feasible extent. But honestly speaking, you need to make the decision. If you choose to keep the athletic performance of the Achilles tendon, it will leave a scar. If you choose minimally invasive surgery, there will not be any problem when you use Achilles tendon in daily life, but there is no best of both worlds.”
President Pei and his wife looked at each other, and their faces showed uncertainty.
Miao Tansheng was not in a hurry. He just stood aside and waited quietly.
Patients and their family members who hesitated when surgery was right around the corner were the type of people he saw the most.
When it was finally the time for surgery and time to sign the operation consent form, many people who were usually very agreeable would change their minds suddenly.

This situation was even more common in the industry of plastic surgery. Many private hospitals had promotional projects, and their aim was to place the patients and their families in the medical environment and even the operating environment before the discussion so that it would be much easier when it was time for the discussion.
The most extreme case was to push the patient onto the operating table before they talked about the price, and this was naturally beneficial in every way possible.
“You decide. After all, our daughter listens to you.” President Pei gave up his right very quickly.
President Pei’s wife looked conflicted, and she complained. “You’re turning me into the scapegoat at this moment?”
“Our daughter listens to you.”
President Pei’s wife thought for a long while before she shook her head and said, “We’d better go for open surgery.”
“Have you decided?” Miao Tansheng took out the document and let them sign.
President Pei’s wife picked a pen, sighed, and said, “She doesn’t look really good too, so if she can’t get married in the future, it’s certainly not because of the scars on her leg.”
After she finished speaking, she signed her name on the informed consent form.

Miao Tansheng made President Pei sign the form before he put it away and gave them further instructions. “We will arrange a car to pick her up for examination, so Miss Pei should get ready early in the morning tomorrow. When our car arrives, she can just leave for the examination.”
“How long does it take for the examination?”

“It’s mainly a MRI scan. We will arrange it to be done in the Third People’s Hospital of Yun Hua City or Fourth People’s Hospital of Yun Hua City, and the normal routine blood test for admittance will be easier...” Miao Tansheng spoke for more than ten minutes before he sent President Pei and his wife away.
When he went back to the clinic and took his seat to rest for a while, the newly booked patients and family members had arrived at his doorstep.
“I’m too busy.” Doctor Miao showed off to Doctor Xiong, who napped in the room.
Doctor Xiong who was woken up did not even look at him. He quietly took out his phone and sent a message to Ling Jiezhou. [I need a raise.]

“Our daughter listens to you.”
President Pei’s wife thought for a long while before she shook her head and said, “We’d better go for open surgery.”
“Have you decided?” Miao Tansheng took out the document and let them sign.
President Pei’s wife picked a pen, sighed, and said, “She doesn’t look really good too, so if she can’t get married in the future, it’s certainly not because of the scars on her leg.”
After she finished speaking, she signed her name on the informed consent form.
Miao Tansheng made President Pei sign the form before he put it away and gave them further instructions.
“We will arrange a car to pick her up for examination, so Miss Pei should get ready early in the morning tomorrow.
When our car arrives, she can just leave for the examination.”
“How long does it take for the examination?”
“It’s mainly a MRI scan.

We will arrange it to be done in the Third People’s Hospital of Yun Hua City or Fourth People’s Hospital of Yun Hua City, and the normal routine blood test for admittance will be easier...” Miao Tansheng spoke for more than ten minutes before he sent President Pei and his wife away.
When he went back to the clinic and took his seat to rest for a while, the newly booked patients and family members had arrived at his doorstep.
“I’m too busy.” Doctor Miao showed off to Doctor Xiong, who napped in the room.
Doctor Xiong who was woken up did not even look at him.
He quietly took out his phone and sent a message to Ling Jiezhou.
[I need a raise.]

chapters.title: Chapter 991: Beating Around the Bush
paragraphs: Ling Ran got off work on time. He returned home for dinner and prepared to start operating on patients again.

For the past few days, Ling Ran had been alternating between working in the hospital for two days and taking a day off. He would be away for the hospital for two or three days a week, and during these off days, he would either be working in his family clinic or going for freelance surgeries.

This was normal for ordinary senior doctors, especially those who were rather renowned. Not only could they earn some extra income by performing freelance surgeries on their off days, but they could also put in some practice so that their skills would not get rusty.

Ling Ran agreed with this way of life. When it came to hepatectomy, which was the surgery he most commonly performed, he was able to reach a new level courtesy of his own efforts. As for other surgeries such as finger replantation surgery, Achilles tendon repair, splenectomy, and orchiectomy, there were very few ways for him to level those skills up.

Compared with other surgical methods, Ling Ran was relatively skilled at Achilles tendon repair surgery. Hence, by continuing to bring in patients with damaged Achilles tendons to Lower Groove Clinic, Ling Ran was able to continuously improve his skills.
“Doctor Ling, you’re back.” Miao Tansheng was the first one who headed out to welcome Ling Ran when he heard the engine of Ling Ran’s Volkswagen Jetta.
“Yeah. Have you gotten the patient ready yet?” The first thing Ling Ran asked Miao Tansheng about when he saw him was the surgery that would be carried out soon.
“About that... Doctor Ling, do you want to have some soup first? Madam Tao made a huge pot of okra soup today and treated all of us to it...”

Ling Ran stopped in his tracks. He knew very well that Miao Tansheng was beating around the bush. Back when he was in school, there were often girls who beat around the bush and talk about irrelevant things before revealing their true intention by giving him gifts or even love letters.
It only took one glance at Miao Tansheng for Ling Ran to know that Miao Tansheng was hiding something from him.
“Just get straight to the point.” Ling Ran was a straightforward person. “Be brief,” he said.
Miao Tansheng looked rather exasperated as he said, “In short, the patient ran away.”
“Ran away?” Ling Ran did not expect things to turn out this way. He asked, “Isn’t the patient a sixteen-year-old teenage girl?”
“Yes.”

“Does this count as running away from home?” Ling Ran did not expect Miao Tansheng to give an answer to this question. He continued, “Has the patient been found yet? Did you guys make a police report?”
“Yes.” Miao Tansheng shrugged and sighed. “But that’s the problem.”
“Yeah?”

“Now, the patient’s family members are saying that they intend to consult doctors from other hospitals to get a second opinion.” After Miao Tansheng told Ling Ran everything, he felt a little more relaxed. He added in an obsequious manner, “I reckon that the patient wants a small incision and a strong Achilles tendon at the same time.”
Ling Ran did not comment on this. He merely asked, “Did you explain things to them?”

Miao Tansheng explained anxiously, “Yes, over the phone. Because I was only able to communicate with them over the phone. I’ve also warned them that they should not consult doctors the same way they go shopping and that they could not just keep making comparisons between different doctors. But they insisted upon it. They were pretty polite, but they refused to send their daughter over for surgery.”

“It’s okay if she doesn’t want to receive surgery.” After listening to what Miao Tansheng said, Ling Ran understood what was going on. He whipped out his phone and said, “If there’re no more patients arranged for tonight, I’ll start gaming.”
“Sure... About this... are you angry?” Miao Tansheng shut his eyes, and he was prepared to receive a scolding.
If the patient chickened out two days before the surgery, he could have arranged for another patient to receive surgery tonight.
However, because the patient only opted out right before the surgery, there was nothing that Miao Tansheng could do.

Ling Ran shook his head. “It’s normal for patients to change their minds. Aside from this, it’s also very risky for this sixteen-year-old to undergo surgery with a large incision. She might not have made a wrong choice by opting out of it.”
“Huh? It’s very risky?”

“Yeah. The patient’s Achilles tendon is relatively short, and her bones and muscles aren’t exactly well-positioned either. Hence, she’s certainly not a very talented dancer. It would be quite risky for her to attempt to reach great heights when it comes to dancing.” As Ling Ran spoke, he tapped on the icon for Kings of Glory on his phone. He then continued, “It might be a more suitable choice for her to opt for minimally invasive Achilles tendon repair so that scarring can be minimized. She can then develop a new hobby.”
Miao Tansheng widened his eyes. “I’m surprised that you didn’t say this to the patient’s family members when you meet them.”

“Talent is not directly proportional to achievements.” Ling Ran shook his head. “A person being untalented doesn’t mean that she can’t achieve great things. The patient obviously suffered from this injury because the quality of her Achilles tendon isn’t the best. It’s relatively short, and it is not very strong either. It might precisely because she isn’t talented enough that she practiced so hard until her Achilles tendon ruptured.”
Miao Tansheng muttered to himself, “For some reason, what you have just said makes a lot of sense. I...”
Ling Ran had already lowered his head, and he was focusing on the game he was playing again.
It was a sunny day with a gentle breeze blowing two days later.
Ling Ran had just arrived at the hospital, and he was enjoying porridge with sixteen side dishes that Tian Qi sent over. This was when the screen of his phone lit up.
“The king asked me to patrol the mountains...”
The voice of the singer was loud and clear, and he immediately lost the mood to eat.
“Hello.” Ling Ran had no choice but to put down his chopsticks and answer the call.
“Doctor Ling, I’m Wang Chuanwen.” Wang Chuanwen chuckled as though he was very close with Ling Ran.

Truth be told, Wang Chuanwen and Ling Ran knew each other quite well. Ever since Wang Chuanwen donated a sum of money to the Emergency Medical Center of Yun Hua Hospital, he showed up a lot to supervise the construction progress of the ICU. On the one hand, it was because he did not want the money he donated to go to waste. On the other hand, he was also trying to proactively form a good relationship with the doctors, especially with Ling Ran.
His efforts seemed to be bearing fruit. At the very least, Ling Ran had gotten a lot more used to seeing him.
“What’s the matter?” Ling Ran looked at his porridge as he held his cell phone.

“I have a friend. His daughter is sixteen this year and ruptured her Achilles tendon while dancing. If I’m not mistaken, he had sought treatment from you earlier, but they ended up chickening out...” Wang Chuanwen chuckled a few times and continued, “Now, he wants you to operate on his daughter again, but he’s a little embarrassed about it. As he’s worried that you would not want to take her daughter in anymore, he asked me for help.”
“Is this friend of yours President Pei?” Ling Ran asked.
“Yes. I see that you remember him.”
“Of course. The patient ran away just when I was about to operate on her.” Ling Ran found this patient very creative, and this was why he remembered the incident so well.

Wang Chuanwen immediately regretted calling Ling Ran. He immediately said, “Ah, I didn’t know that something like this happened. Why didn’t President Pei tell me what exactly happened? If I knew, I wouldn’t have helped him out...”
“How’s the patient doing?” Ling Ran cut Wang Chuanwen off.

Wang Chuanwen hesitated for a moment and said, “His daughter isn’t doing too well, and her foot is swollen. She wants minimally invasive Achilles tendon repair, but she wants to be able to continue dancing too. None of the hospitals dared to promise her that.”
“I don’t do minimally invasive Achilles tendon repair surgery,” Ling Ran quickly replied. There were many doctors who knew how to do that, and to Ling Ran, this was not challenging enough.
Wang Chuanwen quickly said, “No, they want to receive the kind of surgery you’re providing...”
“Send her to Yun Hua Hospital first.”
“So, you’re agreeing to it?”
“Yes.” Ling Ran had never been the kind of person who went back on his word.

A sense of satisfaction filled Wang Chuanwen’s heart when he heard what Ling Ran said. He suddenly felt that donating money to the Emergency Medical Center of Yun Hua Hospital was the best decision that he had ever made in his life.

chapters.title: Chapter 992: Convenient
paragraphs: “Thank you, President Wang.” President Pei held Wang Chuanwen’s hand tight and shook it.
“It’s just a small matter. President Pei, don’t worry about it.” Wang Chuanwen chuckled, and he looked so relaxed that he looked as if he was chatting in a club.

President Pei shook his head. “It might be a small matter for you, but it is a matter of life and death for us. If it weren’t for your help, I’d really be at the end of my line. I don’t have anyone I’m close to and is powerful enough in Yun Hua City. I wanted to call a few contacts and register my name under Doctor Ling, but I lost the chance. The doctors I used to know are not willing to help me deliver my message either...”

President Pei now truly realized the pain of not being able to reach for help even when he had enough money in his pocket. He knew about Ling Ran’s Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique, so he deliberately looked for Ling Ran. However, when his daughter and wife decided to look for a second opinion, when he wanted to contact Ling Ran through his former acquaintances, it was no longer as easy as before.

He would need to queue up and make arrangements with Miao Tansheng again, and Miao Tansheng suggested that he should go to other hospitals for medical treatment. It was hard to get a consultation slot for outpatient consultation from Ling Ran in Yun Hua Hospital, and he would need to wait for two days before he could even begin queuing up. If he contacted Ling Ran through Doctor’s Here, he could only get replies from his subordinates.
If it were not for Wang Chuanwen, President Pei’s best option was to go to another hospital for treatment.

However, President Pei was not willing to accept this ending. For the sake of his daughter, he must find the best doctor. For this reason, President Pei asked for help from all his friends and finally got help from Wang Chuanwen.
If it had to be said, President Pei was truly grateful to Wang Chuanwen, and it was obvious from the way he shook his hand in that handshake.

Wang Chuanwen discreetly freed his hand from President Pei’s, smiled again, and said, “We’re friends, we can talk about this later on. Go to your daughter and wife first. After the surgery, we can have a reunion when we are free.”

“Alright, alright. There are no words that can express my appreciation for your great help. Let’s get together later and have a good chat,” President Pei agreed. He was really anxious to see his daughter and wife now. If he did not have to thank Wang Chuanwen, he would not care to see anyone else.
Wang Chuanwen laughed a couple of times. He had helped a lot of people in his life, but it was rare for him to be able to lend a hand to someone so smoothly and comfortably.
In the past, if he wanted to do a major favor that was related to a life and death situation for others, he had to use massive resources and took some risks.
He would never be able to settle this sort of issue with just a phone call.
Of course, before the call, Wang Chuanwen made some sacrifices. But in terms of the end result, he could be considered to have given extra help to President Pei.
“President Wong, please excuse me.” President Pei took Wang Chuanwen’s hand tightly again and shook it a few times before he ran to the surgery waiting area.
Wang Chuanwen stared after President Pei and smiled profoundly.

In the meeting room, Pei Baoer sat in a wheelchair with one foot up. She looked at Ling ran, and her heart was full of regret. She stared at Ling Ran, lowered her head, and typed furiously on her phone. [Gossips are too unreliable nowadays. How could you describe Doctor Ling as handsome? He should be said to be ethereally handsome, okay?]
[Is he really that handsome?] Best Friend A replied quickly on the phone.
Best Friend B soon texted. [You’re really weak now, so even a dog would look handsome to you.]

Best friend C texted. [That’s why many of the news about people meeting handsome doctors in hospitals are sent out by patients. If the patients think the doctors are handsome, the patients’ family members might not share the same thought, let alone the people unrelated to them.]

[I’ll send you a picture of him. I took it in secret just now.] Pei Baoer sent a picture that she had prepared for a long time. When Ling Ran entered the door, Pei Baoer secretly took the picture. She knew that her best friends would not understand the concept of someone being ethereally handsome. This was just like how she and her best friends had never searched online for pictures of handsome doctors when they heard about how handsome a certain doctor was from Yun Hua Hospital.

After all, there were all kinds of Adonises debuting now. Before their popularity faded away, another batch of handsome men would appear, and all sorts of handsome men with different personalities filled the Internet. If she searched for each handsome man who made the news, Pei Baoer and the others would not have time to do anything else—although they did not have anything to do now.
The “Aluminium Sisters” suddenly became speechless, they stopped chatting in an instance.
Pei Baoer moved her toes proudly before she scowled in pain.
“Baoer, are you not feeling well?” The first thing Pei Baoer’s mother did was look at her daughter. Her voice was filled with great concern.

“I’m fine.” Pei Baoer puffed out her chest and took a deep breath to make her stomach smaller in great determination. She was unlike before, where she behaved as timidly as a mouse. She rubbed her mother’s palm and leaned against her shoulder...
“If there is no problem, let’s move on to the surgery.” Ling Ran ended the preoperative instructions.
President Pei and his family repeated, “No problem. We’ll entrust her to you, Doctor Ling.”
“Your daughter’s surgery will be the first in the afternoon,” Ling Ran said a few more words. He nodded and left with Zuo Cidian.
Pei Baoer quickly took out her phone, snapped a few more photos, and sent them to the group.
“You don’t have to send them anymore. I found a lot of his pictures on the Internet.” Best Friend A started to share the pictures.
“I have high definition ones.” Best Friend B started to share more pictures.
“I have the link and password.” Best Friend C started to copy and paste a link.
Pei Baoer pursed her lips. She snorted and typed quickly. “I have the latest ones.”
“Baoer, stop playing with your phone. I will hold it for you.” As Pei Baoer’s mother continued speaking, she began to cry. She wiped her tears with her hands, but new tears flowed down.
“Come now... why are you crying?” It was hard for President Pei to bear looking at her, and he sounded distressed.

“It’s still a surgery, regardless of whether it’s major or minor...” Pei Baoer’s mother started saying. When she realized that her daughter was still with her, she wiped her tears and said to Pei Baoer, “Don’t be afraid, I’m just worried. Be obedient once you go into the operating theater. By the way, you are the first in line for surgery in the afternoon. Being the first in line is good. The doctors and nurses are full of energy. They will be able to notice every single problem that occurs...”
Pei Baoer nodded with an ignorant look on her face.

“We have to thank President Wang properly after we get back.” Since she was the mother, she did not want her daughter to worry, so she deliberately diverted Pei Baoer’s attention by adding this sentence.

“Of course.” President Pei sighed and said, “President Wang’s factory has always been in quite a tense situation. When it’s time, I will ask if they need any help. In fact, some people from the chamber of commerce want to sell some land, which means that they are just waiting for the good price before they sell it...”

He did not say anything else. He turned to his daughter and said, “Baoer, don’t be afraid. I told you before that Doctor Ling is the best tendon repair surgeon in our country. He is also one of the best in the world. You don’t have to think about anything or do anything...”
“Okay.” Pei Baoer looked incredibly obedient at that moment, and she also felt inexplicably relaxed and... excited.

“Baoer, are you not feeling well?” The first thing Pei Baoer’s mother did was look at her daughter.
Her voice was filled with great concern.
“I’m fine.” Pei Baoer puffed out her chest and took a deep breath to make her stomach smaller in great determination.
She was unlike before, where she behaved as timidly as a mouse.
She rubbed her mother’s palm and leaned against her shoulder...
“If there is no problem, let’s move on to the surgery.” Ling Ran ended the preoperative instructions.
President Pei and his family repeated, “No problem.
We’ll entrust her to you, Doctor Ling.”
“Your daughter’s surgery will be the first in the afternoon,” Ling Ran said a few more words.
He nodded and left with Zuo Cidian.
Pei Baoer quickly took out her phone, snapped a few more photos, and sent them to the group.
“You don’t have to send them anymore.
I found a lot of his pictures on the Internet.” Best Friend A started to share the pictures.
“I have high definition ones.” Best Friend B started to share more pictures.
“I have the link and password.” Best Friend C started to copy and paste a link.
Pei Baoer pursed her lips.
She snorted and typed quickly.
“I have the latest ones.”
“Baoer, stop playing with your phone.
I will hold it for you.” As Pei Baoer’s mother continued speaking, she began to cry.
She wiped her tears with her hands, but new tears flowed down.
“Come now... why are you crying?” It was hard for President Pei to bear looking at her, and he sounded distressed.
“It’s still a surgery, regardless of whether it’s major or minor...” Pei Baoer’s mother started saying.
When she realized that her daughter was still with her, she wiped her tears and said to Pei Baoer, “Don’t be afraid, I’m just worried.
Be obedient once you go into the operating theater.
By the way, you are the first in line for surgery in the afternoon.
Being the first in line is good.
The doctors and nurses are full of energy.
They will be able to notice every single problem that occurs...”
Pei Baoer nodded with an ignorant look on her face.

“We have to thank President Wang properly after we get back.” Since she was the mother, she did not want her daughter to worry, so she deliberately diverted Pei Baoer’s attention by adding this sentence.
“Of course.” President Pei sighed and said, “President Wang’s factory has always been in quite a tense situation.
When it’s time, I will ask if they need any help.
In fact, some people from the chamber of commerce want to sell some land, which means that they are just waiting for the good price before they sell it...”
He did not say anything else.
He turned to his daughter and said, “Baoer, don’t be afraid.
I told you before that Doctor Ling is the best tendon repair surgeon in our country.
He is also one of the best in the world.
You don’t have to think about anything or do anything...”
“Okay.” Pei Baoer looked incredibly obedient at that moment, and she also felt inexplicably relaxed and... excited.

chapters.title: Chapter 993: A Doctor’s Job
paragraphs: As Pei Baoer was wheeled into the operating theater, there were many things on her mind. All of them were fleeting thoughts that came and went.

The thing that had echoed in her mind the most was the joke her best friend made: The tremendously handsome Doctor Ling would be cutting your foot open, fish out your Achilles tendon, and squash it to pieces with his hand...
Due to that, Pei Baoer’s imagination ran wild. It was to the point that everything in the operating theater seemed unreal.
The cloth in the operating theater was dark blue.
The curtains in the operating theater were dark green.
The people in the operating theater were...
“Where’s Doctor Ling?” Pei Baoer suddenly became a little anxious. She looked around and tried to figure out which mask-covered face belonged to Doctor Ling.
In reality, she could tell based on their body structure that none of them were Doctor Ling.

“Doctor Ling is the chief surgeon, so he’ll only come over after we have prepared everything.” Wang Jia was the circulating nurse today, and she had met many silly girls like this. She could not help but smile and say, “Don’t tell me that you sought treatment from Doctor Ling because he’s handsome.”
Pei Baoer glanced at Wang Jia in disdain and said, “Do you think that everyone who seeks him out gets to be operated by him? My father only managed to get him to operate on me through connections.”
She was solemnly trying to convey the fact that she was a rich and beautiful woman who was so rich that her family owned a mine through her expression and words.

Wang Jia pursed her lips and smiled. “I don’t care whether you’re here through connections or because Doctor Ling is handsome. It doesn’t matter, as Doctor Ling is the best doctor in the world when it comes to Achilles tendon repair surgery.”

“Even my father, who likes to boast about things, only dared to say that he’s one of the top surgeons.” Pei Baoer refuted Wang Jia’s statement out of habit. She then looked around, pouted, and said, “I’m not saying that Doctor Ling isn’t the best in the world. I’m just saying that—”
“We should be more humble about it?” Wang Jia spoke as she smiled and looked through the patient’s examination report, body temperature report, surgery consent form, and anesthesia consent form.
This was part of the procedure. More often than not, nothing would go wrong, but nurses could never be too careful about things.

As Pei Baoer lay on the operating table, she was suddenly in the mood to chat. “I’m just saying that since Doctor Ling is the best in the world when it comes to Achilles tendon repair surgery, why can’t he make the incision smaller so that the scar will be smaller? All the excellent doctors I see on TV can perform incredible feats. Doctors like Doctor Ling should be even more incredible, shouldn’t it...?”
Wang Jia glanced at Pei Baoer and said uncertainly, “You’re an athlete, aren’t you? Why else would you choose to receive an open Achilles tendon repair surgery?”
“Dancer. I’m a dance student.” Pei Baoer solemnly corrected Wang Jia.
Wang Jia immediately realized the reason behind Pei Baoer’s decision. “No wonder. Of course, a dancer would mind having a scar.”
“Female athletes are girls too,” Pei Baoer said innocently.

Wang Jia’s emotions were not affected at all as she gazed at Pei Baoer’s face. “This is how medical technology is like. You have no choice but to receive open Achilles tendon repair surgery since you want a strong Achilles tendon. If you were to care about nothing but the aesthetics, you could have opted for minimally invasive surgery... Actually, you’ve made the right choice. You know, the scar will fade, but the dancing skills you obtain and the experience of participating in competitions will always stay with you, don’t you think so?”

“My mom said the same.” Pei Baoer sighed. She then smiled at Wang Jia and said, “By the way, big sister, can you tell Doctor Ling to make my incision a little smaller and make the stitches less obvious when he’s stitching my wound?”
“So, you want the scar to be as small as possible, and for the stitches not to be obvious. Am I right?”
“Yeah.”
“Didn’t you tell Doctor Ling that when you talked to him before the surgery?” Wang Jia did not agree to her request and asked her a question instead.

Pei Baoer pouted. “Everything’s good about Doctor Ling, but he’s such a prim and proper person. He could have pretended to agree to it. I wouldn’t blame him even if he doesn’t stick to his promise...”

Wang Jia was exasperated. “Since you’ve already spoken to Doctor Ling and he didn’t agree to it, what’s the point in asking me to tell him that? Or do you want me to pretend to agree to your request?”
“Is it really not possible?” Pei Baoer was quite concerned about having a large scar. Of course, she cared more about being able to dance.

Wang Jia threw her hands up in exasperation and said, “The exact size of your incision depends on the condition of your Achilles tendon, and the surgeon cannot just stitch up your incision the way you want it to be. If it’s possible, Doctor Ling will definitely make it look as good as possible. Truth be told, based on your circumstances, I can tell you that you definitely made the best choice by seeking treatment from Doctor Ling.”

As Wang Jia spoke, she was paying attention to Pei Baoer’s calf. Because the surgery was delayed a few days, the condition of Pei Baoer’s calf was rather bad. It might even cause her to need a bigger incision than usual.
However, as she had told Pei Baoer, she had definitely made the best choice by wanting Ling Ran to operate on her.
*Swish.*
Someone opened the door of the operating theater, and Pei Baoer immediately looked up excitedly. However, a few nerdy doctors were the ones who entered the operating theater instead.
“Isn’t Doctor Ling the one who will be operating on me?” Pei Baoer was almost screaming.
“The anesthetist is here,” Wang Jia explained.
“Why are there so many anesthetists?” Pei Baoer curled up uneasily. “How long do you guys plan to knock me out?”

“The rest of them are doctors who are here to observe the surgery,” Wang Jia explained with a smile. “Doctors from many hospitals are interested in learning about Achilles tendon repair from Doctor Ling. This is why there are often people visiting the operating theater when he’s working. You don’t mind, do you?”

“Not really.” Pei Baoer looked around at the people in the room. She then craned her head and asked, “How about Doctor Ling? When is he coming? Don’t tell me that he’ll only come over after I’m under anesthetics.”
“Doctor Ling will position you with the help of Doctor Su before Doctor Su administers anesthetics,” Wang Jia explained.
Pei Baoer immediately blushed, and various s*xual positions that she had seen on explicit images and porn videos immediately appeared in her mind.
*Swish.*
Ling Ran entered the operating theater.
All the doctors in the operating theater looked at him.
Ling Ran raised his hands and put on a pair of scrubs with the help of a nurse.
Ma Yanlin walked in after him. He tore open the plastic wrapping around a pair of scrubs and quickly put them on.

Pei Baoer could sense the tense atmosphere in the operating theater and merely looked anxiously at Ling Ran with yearning. Ling Ran was standing not far away from her, and she could basically smell his hormones in the air. It was as if the ventilating system of the operating theater was no longer working.
“Relax your body and lay on your stomach.” Ling Ran’s voice rang out from beside her.
Pei Baoer immediately did as she said, and she kept screaming internally, ‘Doctor Ling has such a pleasant voice! I hope he speaks more.’
Soon, Ling Ran’s voice rang out again.
“Go ahead and administer anesthetics.”
Before Pei Baoer realized what was going on, she started losing consciousness.
“We’re performing Achilles tendon repair surgery with a small incision today,” Ling Ran said calmly only after the patient lost her consciousness entirely.
Ma Yanlin, who was carrying out the preoperative preparations, froze. “Aren’t we using the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique?”

“Something similar, but I made some changes.” Ling Ran paused for a moment and continued, “I had a discussion with Academician Zhu, and we came to the conclusion that open Achilles tendon repair surgery with a small incision could be quite valuable to some. For example, this patient of ours wants to continue dancing after the surgery. Her occupation and lifestyle mean that she needs a small scar. Hence, what she needs are a strong Achilles tendon and a smaller incision.”

Ling Ran explained things in detail, and the other people who were participating in the surgery naturally had no objection. Of course, since Ling Ran was the chief surgeon, all the other medical staff members would definitely go along with everything he said. If some other attending physician or senior resident doctor were the ones breaking the protocol that had been agreed upon, the other medical staff members would have cursed him to death.
After the surgery began, Ma Yanlin struck up a conversation with Ling Ran. “Doctor Ling, did you specially modify the steps of this surgery because of this patient?”
“I guess so. If it goes well, we can continue promoting this new surgical method.”
“You didn’t reveal anything about it beforehand at all. I thought that we would be using the normal Zhu-Ling Achilles Tendon Repair...”
“The surgery might not be successful with a small incision. If it fails, we’ll have to expand the incision and go according to the original plan.” Ling Ran’s voice was loud and clear.
Ma Yanlin immediately understood. “I see. You did this so that the patient’s expectation wouldn’t be too high. But you did come out with the best solution for this young woman’s plight...”
When Wang Jia heard what Ma Yanlin said, she could not help but feel a surge of warmth in her heart.
All the other doctors in the operating theater were touched too.

“Let’s carry on with the surgery.” Ling Ran did not look at any of them, and he continued operating on the patient. “The plan would only be considered successful if the surgery is completed smoothly.”
“So, you’ve indeed come out with the best solution for this young woman’s plight.”
“Isn’t this a doctor’s job?” Again, Ling Ran spoke without raising his head. There was not even the slightest change in his tone of voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 994: Pork Brains
paragraphs: The incision made by Ling Ran today was only one-third of the usual ones he made, which was about two inches in length.

Compared with minimally invasive surgery, an incision like this was still a very huge wound, and it was still very difficult to control the post-surgery scar healing. However, compared with large incisions of more than five inches, which were commonly made in the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique, incisions that were two inches long could still be covered by various methods.
Of course, the most important of these was the strength of the Achilles tendon after the surgery.

If the patient did not pursue strength in the Achilles tendon to ensure corresponding motor ability, the patient would not need to take on the challenge of undergoing the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique and receive a large incision. She could just go straight for minimally invasive surgery.

As a result, Ling Ran always faced patients who belonged to two extremes. At one extreme, there were athletes and sports enthusiasts placed first importance on their motor ability. At another extreme, there were non-professionals more concerned about their wound and appearance, and they could give up some motor ability.
Pei Baoer then revealed to Ling Ran another type of demand, the type that fell in between the two extremes.

On the one hand, she needed her Achilles tendon to have extremely strong motor ability, because dancers really required it. On the other hand, she needed the scars on her legs to be as small as possible and the skin to be as smooth and complete as possible because dancers also really needed their skin to look good.
Just reaching either one of these goals would be extremely detrimental to Pei Baoer’s career; this was a contradiction that was rare in other patients.

Ling Ran had performed Achilles tendon repairs for many female athletes, and among them were young female athletes who had beautiful and smooth skin. But even if they were not willing to have a huge incision, they would eventually make a rational choice to undergo Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique or just simply retire.

However, Pei Baoer was first willing to escape reality by sitting in a wheelchair without undergoing surgery. Then, she endured the pain and returned to the operating table voluntarily, which showed her psychological dilemma.
Ling Ran never cared about what others said, but cared more about what others did.

Approaching Pei Baoer’s situation made Ling Ran become aware of how to further improve the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique, or rather, he became aware of another sort of demand for the Achilles tendon repair technique.

The Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique was originally designed according to Liu Weichen’s needs. Liu Weichen was a world-class male track and field athlete. He had extremely high requirements for his Achilles tendon’s strength and no requirements for his calf’s appearance. Therefore, a four-inch or six-inch incision was not a problem for him. As long as his Achilles tendon’s strength was guaranteed, it was enough. If an extra 2 inches meant that it would increase his Achilles tendon’s strength by one percent, he was willing to go through it.
However, dancers like Pei Baoer obviously needed a balance between both.
In other words, with dancers like Pei Baoer, he could use a new plan and concept to redesign the surgery.
This was unimaginably difficult for ordinary doctors, but for Ling Ran and Academician Zhu, it was not that complicated.
Would it take time to improve a technique? Of course, it would! Would it be a little difficult? Of course, it would! Could it be done? Of course, it could!
Ling Ran lowered his head and sutured the blood vessels gracefully.

The core of the new technique was still blood supply. To be precise, this was the core of the Achilles tendon repair technique. Only by ensuring blood supply could the strength of the Achilles tendon be maintained. In fact, for ordinary doctors, only by ensuring blood supply could the Achilles tendon’s vitality and success of the operation be guaranteed.
However, different surgical methods produced great differences when it came to ensuring blood flow.

Minimally invasive surgery could cause the least wound on the skin, and the blood vessels that were lost during the surgery would be given up by all involved in the surgery in a tacit agreement. As long as the reconnection of the Achilles tendon was completed, the remaining blood vessels would be used to maintain a certain degree of motor ability to ensure that the patient could live a normal life. That was the goal of the surgery.

Open surgery had another direction. It was more of a reconstruction of the system surrounding the Achilles tendon. If the Achilles tendon was ruptured, then everything would need to be sutured back in place. Whenever there was insufficient blood supply, one had to suture the blood vessels and even perform a blood vessel transplant...

The Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique was the best in this regard. It would try not to miss out on even the small blood vessels, which made it more effective and outstanding, but also made it even more difficult. It had almost become a surgery unique to only Ling Ran. The doctors who could perform this kind of suture would rather use it in neurosurgery. They were too lazy to do such an intricate suture on an Achilles tendon.
Ling Ran and Academician Zhu re-discussed the surgery’s design and adopted a plan that could compromise the demands from both sides.

In the case of open surgery with a small incision, the blood vessels should still be sutured as much as possible, but the selection had to be better and had to be focused on the more important ones. If the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique was compared to a sudden downpour of stitches on the ruptured blood vessels, then this suture was irrigation aimed at only the core places.

That was the most stable plan discussed by Academician Zhu and Ling Ran within a short time. However, if they were to really look into it, the length of time did not play into a major factor behind why they could only come up with this plan. Clinical medicine was not like natural science, in which the scientist could take his sweet time to come up with various best plans. Clinical medicine often forced the surgeon to perform surgery because they had no other alternative. The time taken to wait for the right patient was often longer than the time needed for the doctor to design a plan. It was also not uncommon for them to revise a plan when they were about to conduct the surgery.

Pei Baoer was very suited for this modified version of the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique. Not only did she have realistic and exact requirements, but from the MRI scan and other imaging information, her Achilles tendon’s physical conditions were also suited for the surgery.
Ling Ran grabbed a ruptured end of Pei Baoer’s Achilles tendon and nodded with satisfaction while trimming it.

A ruptured Achilles tendon was hairy. In medical terms, it was described as a horsetail, but Pei Baoer’s Achilles tendon was not completely ruptured; less than a quarter of it remained connected. The ruptured part was also not in a uniform shape. So, it was not really like a horsetail but was more like chicken feathers. Some of the thicker ends were like plumage, and some were thin like down feathers. It was a mess.
Ling Ran tidied them up patiently before he began suturing it. After that, he sutured the blood vessels, which varied in thickness. He also focused on protecting the key blood vessels.

Since this was a two-inch incision, the surgeon would have to face a lot of problems regardless of whether it was suturing the Achilles tendon or suturing the blood vessels. To a certain extent, this actually increased the surgery’s difficulty.
However, since there were fewer blood vessels that needed to be sutured, the total operation time could be reduced. From this perspective, the difficulty of the surgery was reduced.

After all, no matter how difficult it was, it was just an orthopedic surgery. Besides needing to pay attention to infection, an orthopedic surgery’s overall difficulty could not be any higher. It was difficult to suture the blood vessels, but it was not more difficult than a craniocerebral surgery; it would take a long time to suture blood vessels, but it was not as long as a craniocerebral surgery; there were a lot of problems when it came to suturing blood vessels, but it was not as complicated as a craniocerebral surgery...

Ling Ran demanded himself to perform by the standards of a neurocranial surgery while performing the Achilles tendon repair surgery. Besides the corresponding equipment not being able to compare to a neurocranial surgery, his assistants’ technique not comparing to the assistants in a neurocranial surgery, and the people were not as careful as those performing a neurocranial surgery... the environment was basically the same.
Ling Ran operated silently. He held an Achilles tendon in one hand and sutured the blood vessels in the other.
Somewhat, it felt a little lonely... Especially when the atmosphere in the operating theater was always lacking in seriousness.

Ma Yanlin, who was accustomed to Ling Ran’s operating theater, was now talking about Lu Wenbin’s pork trotter, “Pork is indeed expensive, but the price of Lu Wenbin’s pork trotters is rising too fast. The price is adjusted once a week, and the magnitude of the price adjustment every week is not low as well. Seriously, he really doesn’t want to suffer the slightest bit of loss when it comes to this business.

sentences.text: The incision made by Ling Ran today was only one-third of the usual ones he made, which was about two inches in length.
Compared with minimally invasive surgery, an incision like this was still a very huge wound, and it was still very difficult to control the post-surgery scar healing.

However, compared with large incisions of more than five inches, which were commonly made in the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique, incisions that were two inches long could still be covered by various methods.
Of course, the most important of these was the strength of the Achilles tendon after the surgery.

If the patient did not pursue strength in the Achilles tendon to ensure corresponding motor ability, the patient would not need to take on the challenge of undergoing the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique and receive a large incision.
She could just go straight for minimally invasive surgery.
As a result, Ling Ran always faced patients who belonged to two extremes.
At one extreme, there were athletes and sports enthusiasts placed first importance on their motor ability.
At another extreme, there were non-professionals more concerned about their wound and appearance, and they could give up some motor ability.
Pei Baoer then revealed to Ling Ran another type of demand, the type that fell in between the two extremes.
On the one hand, she needed her Achilles tendon to have extremely strong motor ability, because dancers really required it.
On the other hand, she needed the scars on her legs to be as small as possible and the skin to be as smooth and complete as possible because dancers also really needed their skin to look good.
Just reaching either one of these goals would be extremely detrimental to Pei Baoer’s career; this was a contradiction that was rare in other patients.
Ling Ran had performed Achilles tendon repairs for many female athletes, and among them were young female athletes who had beautiful and smooth skin.
But even if they were not willing to have a huge incision, they would eventually make a rational choice to undergo Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique or just simply retire.
However, Pei Baoer was first willing to escape reality by sitting in a wheelchair without undergoing surgery.
Then, she endured the pain and returned to the operating table voluntarily, which showed her psychological dilemma.
Ling Ran never cared about what others said, but cared more about what others did.

Approaching Pei Baoer’s situation made Ling Ran become aware of how to further improve the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique, or rather, he became aware of another sort of demand for the Achilles tendon repair technique.
The Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique was originally designed according to Liu Weichen’s needs.
Liu Weichen was a world-class male track and field athlete.
He had extremely high requirements for his Achilles tendon’s strength and no requirements for his calf’s appearance.
Therefore, a four-inch or six-inch incision was not a problem for him.
As long as his Achilles tendon’s strength was guaranteed, it was enough.
If an extra 2 inches meant that it would increase his Achilles tendon’s strength by one percent, he was willing to go through it.
However, dancers like Pei Baoer obviously needed a balance between both.
In other words, with dancers like Pei Baoer, he could use a new plan and concept to redesign the surgery.
This was unimaginably difficult for ordinary doctors, but for Ling Ran and Academician Zhu, it was not that complicated.
Would it take time to improve a technique?
Of course, it would!
Would it be a little difficult?
Of course, it would!
Could it be done?
Of course, it could!
Ling Ran lowered his head and sutured the blood vessels gracefully.
The core of the new technique was still blood supply.
To be precise, this was the core of the Achilles tendon repair technique.
Only by ensuring blood supply could the strength of the Achilles tendon be maintained.
In fact, for ordinary doctors, only by ensuring blood supply could the Achilles tendon’s vitality and success of the operation be guaranteed.
However, different surgical methods produced great differences when it came to ensuring blood flow.
Minimally invasive surgery could cause the least wound on the skin, and the blood vessels that were lost during the surgery would be given up by all involved in the surgery in a tacit agreement.

As long as the reconnection of the Achilles tendon was completed, the remaining blood vessels would be used to maintain a certain degree of motor ability to ensure that the patient could live a normal life.
That was the goal of the surgery.
Open surgery had another direction.
It was more of a reconstruction of the system surrounding the Achilles tendon.
If the Achilles tendon was ruptured, then everything would need to be sutured back in place.
Whenever there was insufficient blood supply, one had to suture the blood vessels and even perform a blood vessel transplant...
The Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique was the best in this regard.
It would try not to miss out on even the small blood vessels, which made it more effective and outstanding, but also made it even more difficult.
It had almost become a surgery unique to only Ling Ran.
The doctors who could perform this kind of suture would rather use it in neurosurgery.
They were too lazy to do such an intricate suture on an Achilles tendon.
Ling Ran and Academician Zhu re-discussed the surgery’s design and adopted a plan that could compromise the demands from both sides.
In the case of open surgery with a small incision, the blood vessels should still be sutured as much as possible, but the selection had to be better and had to be focused on the more important ones.
If the Zhu-Ling Achilles Repair Technique was compared to a sudden downpour of stitches on the ruptured blood vessels, then this suture was irrigation aimed at only the core places.
That was the most stable plan discussed by Academician Zhu and Ling Ran within a short time.
However, if they were to really look into it, the length of time did not play into a major factor behind why they could only come up with this plan.
Clinical medicine was not like natural science, in which the scientist could take his sweet time to come up with various best plans.
Clinical medicine often forced the surgeon to perform surgery because they had no other alternative.
The time taken to wait for the right patient was often longer than the time needed for the doctor to design a plan.
It was also not uncommon for them to revise a plan when they were about to conduct the surgery.

A ruptured Achilles tendon was hairy.
In medical terms, it was described as a horsetail, but Pei Baoer’s Achilles tendon was not completely ruptured; less than a quarter of it remained connected.
The ruptured part was also not in a uniform shape.

It was a mess.

From this perspective, the difficulty of the surgery was reduced.

Besides needing to pay attention to infection, an orthopedic surgery’s overall difficulty could not be any higher.
